summary: Escalating round-reduced attacks on HighwayHash-64 by six methods (hill-climb, sum-cancellation, SMT, weak-key conditioning, high-sample bias, cube/degree), each effect independently reproduced; plus proof-side agents bounding what is provable
logs: Attacking R=1 with 6 methods, 0 seed pairs
Attacking R=2 with 6 methods, 8 seed pairs
Attacking R=3 with 6 methods, 8 seed pairs
Attacking R=4 with 6 methods, 8 seed pairs

synthesis.answer_to_author:
Breakable, with independently reproduced pairs, at R=0, 1, 2; broken as a distinguisher but not by collisions at R=3; nothing detectable at R=4.

R=0: rate 1 for every key for any difference in packet lanes 2,3 (proven: lane locality, z3 UNSAT with symbolic key and packet). R=1: lane 3 byte 0 +-1 collides for 0.996 of keys (4277934604/2^32; five independent reproductions at 2^24), and this is PROVEN as Pr >= 1-9*2^-8 for every 32-byte message (Theorem 1, refereed); two more classes proven >= 0.973 and >= 0.988; five classes proven <= 2^-8..2^-22 (Theorem 2). R=2: the same pair gives full collisions at 2^-19.7 (4998 and 5004 in two runs of 2^32; 298/313/338/331 per 2^28 over bases, seeds and lengths 29..64 B), i.e. 2^44 times the ideal; bit 63 of H(m)^H(m') is set for only 2^-12.2 of keys. The mechanism is identified (a chance coincidence of two product differences staying out of the bytes that reach lane 0; six byte conditions predict 89 of 100 collisions) but the rate has no proof. R=3: 0 full collisions in 2^34.5 keys (rate < 2^-33), yet a clean distinguisher: +-1 in lane 3 byte 5 (message byte 29) sets bit 63 of H(m)^H(m') for 0.421 of keys instead of 1/2 (z = -9927, -10040, -10345 at 2^32 in three lenses, reproduced eight times), the parity of the top two bits of H(m')-H(m) is even for 0.607 of keys, the top 8 output bits agree 2.57x too often, and the sign is the same for every key, so ~2^11 chosen pairs per key (or ~2^11 keys per pair) distinguish H_3 from random. R=4 (published): 0 collisions in 2^34.5 keys for the byte-29 family and 2^33.5 for the byte-24 family (rates < 2^-33 at 95%); per-bit bias < 2^-14.4 and every one of the 65535 linear masks of the top 16 bits < 2^-13.5 at 2^32 keys; partial-collision counts, additive-magnitude counts, joint byte tables, cube/ANF degree profiles to d=26, and the per-key mean-z^2 test are all at their null values; the random control is indistinguishable from every structured pair; nothing inside weak-key classes of density 2^-32 (2^28 keys), 2^-64, 2^-96. So the published design keeps exactly one round of margin against distinguishers and two against full collisions, and every single-packet lever found is erased by the two lane-0 multiplies of round 4, whose operands are wide by then.

What is proven (refereed and confirmed): R=0 lane locality; the R=1 closed form for 32-byte messages; the R=1 zero-multiply sector with two-sided bounds (Theorems 1 and 2, slice lemma); exact one-step separation (a product with a shared operand changes iff its co-operand is nonzero; silencing subspaces of density 2^-32 for 32-byte messages); bijectivity of Update/round/remainder with explicit inverses; and the count that a fully silenced trail through R rounds activates >= R+2 multiplies. Four lemma statements were refuted and corrected by the referees (Lemma 1's 'every collision is a truncation collision' fails for known keys with three-packet differences and holds for single-packet differences; the R=0 carry-model formula for lane-1 bits 16..22; Lemma 3's corollary on the remainder path; Lemma 4's k_msg formula). Nothing is proven about R >= 2.

The dichotomy is decided for R <= 3 (broken; provably so for R <= 1) and undecided for R = 4, and it cannot be decided by sampling: 2^-64 is thirty binary orders below the reach of any key sweep (2^40 keys, ~130 CPU-h, would only move the per-bit bias floor from 2^-14 to 2^-18 and the collision floor to 2^-38), and proof stops three rounds earlier, at the first key-masked 32x32 product on any trail (Proposition 3's equation (M^(P+h))-(M^P)=c, already inside R=1; from R=2 on both operands of the first round-1 multiply differ and even the exact identity a'H-aH=(a'-a)H is gone). What could still move the boundary: on the proof side, a machine-checked structural theorem that every last-packet difference reaches the last round's lane-0 words only through >= 2 key-masked products (a 'no designed trail at R >= 3' theorem), which yields a heuristic trail-cost bound of 2^-8k..2^-32k, never 2^-64; on the attack side, only a new mechanism (a two-packet trail where the second packet cancels the first, or a round-4 statistic predicted from the still-narrow mul1[0] at the round-4 entry), since the byte-29 channel is the only R=3 handle and it dies in one round. The honest sentence for the paper: nothing bounds H_4's collision probability between the measured < 2^-33 and the claimed 2^-64, and nothing found suggests it is above 2^-33.

[any R, refereed CONFIRMED parts of Lemma 3] One-step separation: (a) after v1[i] += delta the low half differs iff lo32(delta) != 0, the high half iff hi32(delta) + carry != 0 mod 2^32; (b) since 32x32->64 products are exact integers, a'H - aH = (a'-a)H vanishes iff H = 0, so mul0[i] changes iff lo32(delta) != 0 and hi32(v0[i]) != 0, and mul1[i] changes iff the high half of v1[i] changes and lo32(v0[i] + mul1[i]) != 0; (c) for one-packet messages and a uniform key the co-operands H and L are independent uniform, P[H=0] = P[L=0] = 2^-32, P[H=L=0] = 2^-64, and for |M| = 32 P[carry] = lo32(delta)/2^32 exactly. The exact silencing subspaces hi32(key[i]) = hi32(init0[i]) and lo32(key[i]) = lo32(init0[i]) ^ (-lo32(init1[i])) hold ONLY for |M| = 32 (referee correction; on the remainder path the subspaces are hi32(v0[i]) = 0 resp. lo32(v0[i]) + lo32(init1[i]) = 0 with v0[i] = (init0[i]^key[i]) + (s<<32) + s).

[any R, refereed CONFIRMED parts of Lemma 4] Silenced trails with the corrected k'_msg(delta) = #{i: lo32(delta_i) != 0} + #{i: hi32(delta_i) not in {0, 2^32-1}} + #{i: lo32(delta_i) = 0 and hi32(delta_i) = 2^32-1} >= 1: the message Update activates >= k'_msg multiplies with exactly one differing operand each, so for one-packet messages P[message Update silenced] <= 2^(-32 k'_msg) <= 2^-32 (checked: 0 silenced in 2^20 uniform keys, 65536/65536 in the density-2^-32 subspace); on a silenced trail round 1 activates >= 2 multiplies in two different lanes (measured minimum 3), every later round >= 1 (33,685,504 state-level round evaluations, minimum 1), so a fully silenced trail through R rounds activates >= R+2 multiplies. The 2^-32(R+2) figures are heuristic and NOT part of the proven statement.

[any R, referee-corrected form of Lemma 1] Update_p, the finalization round rho and the remainder step are bijections of the 1024-bit state with the explicit inverse F^-1, E^-1, D^-1, C^-1, B^-1, A^-1 (65536/65536 checked by both sides); tau = v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0] is a surjective homomorphism with fibres of exactly 2^960 states; for equal-length messages whose padded packet sequences differ in exactly one packet (the setting of this entire study) the final states differ for every key, so every such collision is a collision of tau on two distinct states. The original clause 'for every M != M' the final states differ' is REFUTED (known-key three-packet counterexample) and is not claimed.

[any R, elementary, not refereed] Last-round truncation collision: for every entering state, mul1[0] ^= 2^63 leaves the output unchanged (2^20/2^20 states). Two-line argument re-derived here: step D's product reads lo32(v0[0]) and hi32(v1[0]), neither of which changes (v0[0] changes by exactly 2^63 after step C, v1[0] does not read mul1), so mul1[0] ends XORed by 2^63 = plus 2^63 mod 2^64 and v0[0] ends plus 2^63; ZipperMerge does not route byte 7 of v0[0] into v1[0]; the two 2^63 terms cancel in tau. Its unreachability from a message pair is argued, not proven.
synthesis.unproven_boundary: Proof stops one multiply into the trail, already at R=1, and never recovers. Precisely: (1) At R=1 the zero-multiply sector (differences routed only into v0[3]) is fully decided (Theorems 1, 2). The first multiply-active branch, m' = m + 2^40 e_3 with the 2^-8 of keys where A3.b5 = ff, reduces (claimant's Proposition 3, z3-proved but NOT refereed) to Pr_key[(M ^ (P+h)) - (M ^ P) = 0xFEFF0000FFFFFFFF] with M = mul0[0] = init0[0] ^ (lo32(A0) * hi32(init0[0]^k0)) a key-dependent XOR mask, P = lo32(U0) * hi32(X0) a 32x32 product and h = hi32(X0). Carry analysis forces h odd, 25 bits of M and 24 bits of P; the M pattern was counted exhaustively for ONE m0 (196 of 2^32); nothing bounds it uniformly in m, the non-generic carry sub-cases (wraps in U0, U1, Z3, hi32(Z2)) are not enumerated, and nothing bounds the min-entropy of lo32(U0), i.e. of hi32(Z2) = hi32(B2 + f0(A2, A3)) over (k2, k3) where hi32(k2) enters both B2 and A2 (only 15 bits are certifiable). The certified bound for this pair is therefore 2^-8 + 3*2^-16 against a measured 0 in 2^26.3 keys: a gap of at least 2^18 on the very first active multiply. (2) From R=2 on, every trail crosses Permute and the round-1 multiplies of the differing lane have BOTH operands differing (Lemma 4(b), refereed), so even the exact identity a'H - aH = (a'-a)H is lost: a'H' - aH = (a'-a)H' + a(H'-H) carries no structure that bounds Pr[a'H' = aH], and the XOR masks are key-dependent. No statement about R >= 2 has a proof; the R=2 rate 2^-19.7 has an explanatory mechanism (six byte conditions predict 89 of 100 collisions) but no closed form. (3) The universality-style route fails for structural reasons: f(k) = H_R(k,m) - H_R(k,m') is not a polynomial over Z/2^64 (XOR with key-dependent words, lo/hi splits, byte permutations), Z/2^64 has no root bound even for polynomials (2^63 X vanishes on half the ring, (2^32 X)(2^32 Y) identically), the GF(2) degree of product bits reaches 32 so the Boolean degree bound is vacuous, and the assumption that would finish it, 'products along a trail are independent uniform words', is false (two products sharing an operand differ by exactly (a'-a)H, confined below bit 33 for 75% of keys for delta = 1; P[bit 63 of a product] = 0.153; operands are functions of the same key halves). (4) What the structural lemmas do give beyond R=1 is only a count: a fully silenced trail through R rounds needs >= R+2 zero co-operands (heuristically 2^-32(R+2)), but the observed R <= 2 collisions are NOT silenced trails (they are byte-carry/confinement events at ~2^-8 each), and the analytic lenses' claims that no designed trail exists at R >= 3 (sumcancel-R3/R4 taint pull-back: all 46 R=4 condition bytes polluted for every 1- and 2-byte pattern; weakkey-R3's multiply-free ZipperMerge route into q3[0] that no lane-1 route can cancel) are hand-derived over-approximations, consistent with every measurement, refereed by nobody, and not probability bounds. (5) Sampling cannot cross the boundary from the other side: 2^32..2^34 keys per pair bound per-pair collision rates at 2^-33 and per-bit biases at 2^-14.4 (2^-13.5 per linear mask), which is 30 binary orders above the ideal 2^-64; 2^40 keys would reach 2^-38 / 2^-18. So the truth about H_4 lies strictly between 'no proof beyond R=1' and 'no signal at 2^-33 / 2^-14', and no technique in this panel can narrow that interval.

\section{HighwayHash-64 under round reduction}
\label{app:highway}

HighwayHash-64~\cite{highwayhash} keeps a $1024$-bit state
$(v_0,v_1,m_0,m_1)$ of four $64$-bit lanes each.  One \texttt{Update} with a
$32$-byte packet $p$ does, per lane $i$,
$v_{1,i}\mathrel{+}=m_{0,i}+p_i$,
$m_{0,i}\mathrel{\oplus}=\mathrm{lo}_{32}(v_{1,i})\cdot\mathrm{hi}_{32}(v_{0,i})$,
$v_{0,i}\mathrel{+}=m_{1,i}$,
$m_{1,i}\mathrel{\oplus}=\mathrm{lo}_{32}(v_{0,i})\cdot\mathrm{hi}_{32}(v_{1,i})$,
followed by two additions of a fixed byte permutation (\emph{ZipperMerge})
that mixes lanes $\{0,1\}$ with each other and lanes $\{2,3\}$ with each
other.  The key enters only $v_0,v_1$ at reset; $m_0,m_1$ start at public
constants.  Finalization applies $R=4$ rounds of
$\texttt{Update}(\texttt{Permute}(v_0))$, where \texttt{Permute} rotates the
lanes by two and swaps the $32$-bit halves, and returns
$v_{0,0}+v_{1,0}+m_{0,0}+m_{1,0}$.  We write $H_R$ for the variant with $R$
rounds; $H_4$ is the published function.  The reference C (Apache-2.0) was
copied with one added round-count parameter and reproduces the published
vectors (\texttt{kExpected64} for all $65$ lengths and the $33$-byte
\texttt{kTestKey2} vector) at $R=4$ in every tool.

\paragraph{Model.}
As in \Cref{app:adversarial}: the key is four uniformly random $64$-bit
words, hidden; the attacker fixes a pair of equal-length messages whose
difference lies in the last packet; the reported rate is the fraction of keys
for which the pair collides, or for which a given bit of
$H_R(m)\oplus H_R(m')$ (or of $H_R(m')-H_R(m)$) is set.  A random function
gives $2^{-64}$ and $\tfrac12$; $z$ denotes the deviation of a bit count from
$N/2$ in units of $\sqrt N/2$.  Messages are $32$ bytes unless stated; $29$-,
$48$-, $61$-, $63$- and $64$-byte variants (remainder path, second packet)
were checked for every effect quoted.  Six methods were run at every $R$:
evolutionary search over pairs, analytic cancellation in the lane-$0$ output
sum, exact bit-vector models in z3 and boolector, sampling of the key
subspaces that zero a multiply operand, bias counters at $2^{28}$--$2^{32}$
keys (per bit, all $65535$ linear masks of the top $16$ bits, additive
near-collisions, joint byte tables), and cube/ANF testers.  Every rate below
was re-measured by a second implementation with its own key stream, and every
proof was refereed; refereed statements are marked \emph{proven}, everything
else is a measurement.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}cp{0.34\linewidth}p{0.36\linewidth}l@{}}
\toprule
$R$ & best full-collision rate & best distinguisher & status \\
\midrule
$0$ & $1$: any difference in packet lanes $2,3$ & output identical & proven, all keys \\
$1$ & $0.996$: lane $3$ byte $0$ $\pm1$ ($2^{32}$ keys) & saturated & proven $\ge1-9\cdot2^{-8}$, every $m$ \\
$2$ & $2^{-19.7}$: same pair ($4998$, $5004$ in $2\times2^{32}$) & bit $63$ of $H\oplus H'$ set for $2^{-12.2}$ of keys & measured; mechanism known \\
$3$ & $0$ in $2^{34.5}$ ($<2^{-33}$) & lane $3$ byte $5$ $\pm1$: bit $63$ of $H\oplus H'$ set for $0.421$ of keys ($z=-9927$ at $2^{32}$) & measured; no proof \\
$4$ & $0$ in $2^{34.5}$ ($<2^{-33}$) & none: every bit $|\varepsilon|<2^{-14.4}$, every top-$16$ mask $|\varepsilon|<2^{-13.5}$ ($2^{32}$ keys) & open \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{HighwayHash-64 with $R$ finalization rounds, difference in the last
packet, uniform key.  Rates are per pair over keys; the zeros at $R=3,4$ are
$95\%$ upper bounds $3/N$ over the pairs tested at scale.}
\label{tab:highway:rounds}
\end{table}

\paragraph{$R=0$ and $R=1$ (proven).}
Without finalization the lane pairs never meet: $H_0$ is a function of
$k_0$, $k_1$, the length and the message bytes at positions $32q+j$ with
$j<16$ only, so any difference confined to bytes $16$--$31$ of any packet
collides for every key (z3: \textsc{unsat} with symbolic key and packet,
also with an uninterpreted multiplier; measured $2^{20}/2^{20}$ and, for the
$256$ one-byte messages, $65536/65536$ keys).  With one round, the lane-$0$
output of a $32$-byte message has a closed form in which lanes $2,3$ enter
only through $v_{0,2}$ (which feeds both lane-$0$ multiplies) and $v_{0,3}$
(which feeds byte shuffles and additions only).  Differences routed into
$v_{0,3}$ never touch a multiply, and there everything is decidable: for
\emph{every} $32$-byte $m$, with $e_i$ one unit in packet lane $i$,
\[
\Pr[H_1(m+e_3)=H_1(m)]\ge1-9\cdot2^{-8},\quad
\Pr[H_1(m+2^{32}e_2)=H_1(m)]\ge1-7\cdot2^{-8},\quad
\Pr[H_1(m+2^{56}e_2)=H_1(m)]\ge1-3\cdot2^{-8}
\]
(measured $0.996$, $0.988$, $0.992$), and conversely
$\Pr[H_1(m+2^{8}e_3)=H_1(m)]\le2^{-22}$,
$\Pr[H_1(m+2^{16}e_3)=H_1(m)]\le2^{-8}$,
$\Pr[H_1(m+2^{40}e_3)=H_1(m)]\le2^{-8}+3\cdot2^{-16}$ (measured $0$ in
$2^{26}$ keys each).  The proofs are z3 certificates on a relaxed model in
which seven key-derived words are free (sound for statements that hold for
every key), combined with a counting lemma for single key bytes.  The
two-byte pattern lane $3$ $+\,\texttt{0xFF00}$ collides at
$(255/256)^6=0.9768$ (measured $0.97678$ at $2^{26}$ keys, $0.97684$ and
$0.97676$ in two reproductions): the $+2^{32}$ it delivers to $v_{0,0}$
cancels the $-2^{32}$ it delivers to $v_{1,0}$ while both $m$ words stay
equal, and each of the six failure modes is one byte carry.

\paragraph{$R=2$ (collisions at $2^{-19.7}$).}
The difference $\pm1$ in lane $3$ byte $0$ (message byte $24$) is the one
last-packet pattern that survives the necessary conditions for a cancellation
in the lane-$0$ sum after two rounds.  It collides for $4998$ and $5004$ of
$2^{32}$ keys in two independent runs ($2^{-19.7}$, i.e.\ $2^{44}$ times the
ideal), for $298$, $313$, $338$, $331$ of $2^{28}$ across bases and seeds, and
at the same rate through the remainder path ($29$, $61$, $63$ bytes) and in
the second packet of a $64$-byte message.  Bit $63$ of $H_2(m)\oplus H_2(m')$
is set for only $2^{-12.2}$ of keys, $39$ of the $64$ bits have $|z|\ge6$, and
the low $32$ bits collide for $2^{-10.05}$ of keys.  The colliding keys are a
chance coincidence: the two product differences that the $+1$ creates
($\delta\cdot\mathrm{hi}_{32}(v_{0,3})$ at the packet step and
$\delta\cdot2^{16}\,\mathrm{hi}_{32}(v_{0,1})$ in round $1$) both stay out of
the bytes that reach lane $0$; six byte conditions after round $1$ account for
$89$ of $100$ collisions.  Zeroing the first operand by the key condition
$\mathrm{hi}_{32}(k_3)=\mathrm{hi}_{32}(\mathrm{init}_{0,3})$ (density
$2^{-32}$) raises the rate to $2^{-9.86}$ ($289289/2^{28}$); zeroing the
second as well (density $2^{-64}$) raises it to $0.980$, so that class
contributes $2^{-64}\cdot0.98$ and the unconditional $2^{-19.7}$ is a
carry-and-confinement event, not a weak-key event.  No proof of the rate
exists.

\paragraph{$R=3$ (a distinguisher, no collisions).}
Every $R=3$ effect found lives in one channel: an additive $\pm d$, $d$
small, in lane $3$ byte $5$ (message byte $29$).  For $d=1$ the top bit of
$H_3(m)\oplus H_3(m')$ is set for $0.421$--$0.424$ of keys instead of
$\tfrac12$ ($z=-9927$, $-10040$, $-10345$ at $2^{32}$ keys in three lenses,
$z_{63}\approx-0.15\sqrt N$; bits $57$--$62$ biased with the bias halving per
bit); the parity of the top two bits of $H_3(m')-H_3(m)$ is even for $0.607$
of keys; the top $8$ output bits agree for $2^{-6.64}$ of keys ($2.57\times$
ideal; $2^{-14.62}$ for the top $16$, and the same $2.5$--$2.8\times$ excess of
$|H_3(m')-H_3(m)|<2^k$ for every $k$ from $32$ to $56$); the second derivative
on the two-bit cube $\{\text{lane-}3\text{ bit }0,\text{ bit }40\}$ has top
bit $0$ for $0.685$ of keys ($2^{26}$ keys).  The bias has the same sign for
every key ($64$ of $64$ keys, $z_{63}\in[-166,-151]$ at $2^{20}$ pairs each),
so about $2^{11}$ chosen message pairs distinguish $H_3$ from random under a
fixed key, and about $2^{11}$ keys under a fixed pair.  Any second differing
bit anywhere in the packet kills the effect ($|z|\le3.5$ at $2^{20}$ keys for
$221$ two-bit patterns).  The $R=2$ collision family keeps only a residue at
$R=3$, $\varepsilon\approx-2^{-14}$ on bit $63$ ($z=-10.5$ and $-7.8$ in two
runs of $2^{32}$).  Full collisions: $0$ in $2^{34.5}$ keys over the channel's
variants, i.e.\ below $2^{-33}$.  Key subspaces that silence multiplies
sharpen the bias but never produce an $R=3$ collision: with
$\mathrm{hi}_{32}(k_3)=\mathrm{hi}_{32}(\mathrm{init}_{0,3})$ (density
$2^{-32}$) the lane-$3$ $+1$ pair has $\Pr[\text{bit }63\text{ differs}]=0.434$,
with two further round-$1$ conditions (density $2^{-96}$) $0.016$, and $0$
collisions in $2^{28}$ and $2^{24}$ conditional keys.

\paragraph{$R=4$ (the published function).}
Nothing.  For the byte-$29$ pair at $2^{32}$ keys: $0$ collisions; every bit
of $H_4(m)\oplus H_4(m')$ and of $H_4(m')-H_4(m)$ has $|z|\le3.0$
($|\varepsilon|<2^{-14.4}$); all $65535$ linear masks of the top $16$ bits of
either difference have $|z|\le4.8$ against a null maximum of $4.9$
($|\varepsilon|<2^{-13.5}$); the joint distributions of the top bytes and of
the low bytes of the two outputs are independent ($|z|<1.4$); the counts of
$|H_4(m')-H_4(m)|<2^k$ are at $1.00\times$ ideal for $k=40,\dots,60$.  The same
holds for the $R=2$ collision pair, for the complement pairs $\bar w_3$ and
$\bar w_2\bar w_3$, for $w_0+2^{32}$, $w_3\oplus2^{31}$, $w_0\oplus2^{63}$ and
a random control at $2^{29}$--$2^{32}$ keys, for every winner of four $R=4$
hill-climbs ($577{,}004$ pairs evaluated, $2^{30}$ keys on the top two), for
cube dimensions up to $26$ in message and key bits (every restricted degree
$\ge d-1$, monomial density at random), and inside the weak-key classes of
density $2^{-32}$ ($2^{28}$ keys), $2^{-64}$ and $2^{-96}$
($2^{23}$--$2^{24}$).  With $0$ collisions in $2^{34.5}$ keys for the byte-$29$
family and $2^{33.5}$ for the byte-$24$ family their rates are below
$2^{-33}$; the ideal $2^{-64}$ is thirty binary orders further down.  Against
everything tried here the published design keeps one round of margin against
distinguishers and two against collisions.

\paragraph{Where the proof stops.}
A collision is a zero of $f(k)=H_R(k,m)-H_R(k,m')$ over $\mathbb Z/2^{64}$,
and $f$ is not a polynomial: XOR with key-dependent words, $32$-bit splits
and byte permutations sit between the products, and $\mathbb Z/2^{64}$ has
no root bound anyway ($2^{63}X$ vanishes on half the ring).  The first
obstruction appears at $R=1$, one multiply into the trail: for
$m'=m+2^{40}e_3$ and the $2^{-8}$ of keys with a carry into the multiplied
half, the collision condition is
$(M\oplus(P+h))-(M\oplus P)=\texttt{FEFF0000FFFFFFFF}$ with $M=m_{0,0}$ a
key-dependent XOR mask, $P=L\cdot h$ a $32\times32$ product and $h$ its
key-dependent operand.  Carry analysis pins $25$ bits of $M$ and $24$ of $P$
(an exhaustive count gives $196$ admissible $\mathrm{hi}_{32}(k_0)$ of
$2^{32}$ for one $m_0$), but the count depends on $m$, the remaining
sub-cases are not enumerated, and nothing bounds the entropy of $L$ over
$(k_2,k_3)$; the certified bound for this pair is $2^{-8}+3\cdot2^{-16}$
against a measured $0$ in $2^{26}$.  From $R=2$ on every trail crosses
\texttt{Permute} and meets multiplies with \emph{both} operands differing,
where even the identity $a'H-aH=(a'-a)H$ is lost.  What survives as a theorem
is structural: \texttt{Update}, the round and the remainder step are
permutations of the state with explicit inverses, so a collision of two
messages differing in one packet is a collision of the $64$-bit truncation on
two distinct states; a multiply operand that carries a difference is silenced
only by a zero co-operand ($2^{-32}$ per multiply for one-packet messages);
and a trail through $R$ rounds on which every product is silenced activates
at least $R+2$ multiplies.  The observed $R\le2$ collisions are not of that
kind: they are byte-carry and byte-confinement events at about $2^{-8}$ each,
and no accounting of them beyond $R=2$ has been made exact.  The assumption
that would close the gap, that the products along a trail are independent
uniform words, is false: two products sharing an operand differ by exactly
$(a'-a)H$ (confined below bit $33+\log_2|a'-a|$ for three quarters of the
keys), and the top bit of a product of uniform $32$-bit halves is set with
probability $\tfrac12-\tfrac12\ln2=0.153$, which is the mechanism behind the
$R=3$ bias.

\paragraph{Caveat.}
The differences were confined to the last packet (plus a second packet for
the two families tested at $64$ bytes); two-packet trails in which the second
packet cancels the first were not searched.  Sampling decides rates down to
about $2^{-33}$ per pair and biases down to $2^{-14}$ per bit; $H_4$ is
neither broken nor proven at any finer scale.  For a \emph{known} key the
internal state is not collision resistant at any $R$: since the packet enters
$v_1$ additively and every step is a bijection, one can choose, for any given
key, a $96$-byte pair differing in lane $0$ of three consecutive packets that
reaches the identical $1024$-bit state (verified for $65536/65536$ keys; each
such pair collides for $0/65536$ other keys).  This is why the statements
above are over random keys and single-packet differences.

Kept only in the referee's corrected form (bijectivity; single-packet differences give distinct states), which covers this study's threat model.

Lemma 2 converse and its carry model (proof-trails): the converse ('collides with probability exactly 1 at R=0 only if confined to lanes 2,3') stays a conjecture (witness keys found for all 659 lane-0/1 differences searched, no proof); the carry-model formula (1-2^-(32-b))^2 for lane-1 bits 16..23 is REFUTED for b = 16..22 (z = -23..-96 at 2^26 keys; true rate ~1-3*2^-(32-b), corrected formula fits with |z| <= 1.4).

Lemma 3 corollary (proof-trails): REFUTED on the remainder path (1 <= |M| <= 31): the stated key subspaces do not silence mul0/mul1 there (changed for 2^20/2^20 keys in 24 cells) because UpdateRemainder adds (s<<32)+s to v0 first; holds only for |M| = 32. Parts (a),(b),(c) stand.

Lemma 4(a) k_msg formula (proof-trails): REFUTED by delta = 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 (k_msg = 0 but one multiply is always active); replaced by k'_msg. Lemma 4's heuristic part (P[silenced] <= 2^-32(R+2)) rests on 'independent uniform co-operands in the rounds', which is an assumption, not provable and not refereed; the >= R+2 count is all that is proven.

Lemma 5 (proof-trails, 'where a universality proof stops') and Proposition 3 / the multiply-active conjecture (proof-attempt): not refereed. Lemma 5 is commentary on technique, not a theorem; Proposition 3 is a claimant z3 certificate whose M-pattern count (196/2^32) holds for one m0 only. Both are used here only to locate the boundary, not listed as proven.

sumcancel-R2's literal family (ii) at R=2: REFUTED by sumcancel-R3 (an unabsorbed carry route v0''[0].b5 -> v1''[0].b3 of weight 2^24); the corrected R=0 pair F2b (0.0618 measured vs 0.0613 predicted) is fine but is an R=0 curiosity.

Structural 'impossibility' claims of the analytic lenses: 'delta = +-1 is the ceiling of the R=2 channel', 'no designed R=3 trail exists', 'the R=4 conditions strictly contain the R=3 conditions plus six mul-word conditions', weakkey-R3's ZipperMerge-route obstruction: hand-derived byte-taint over-approximations (carries ignored, signs untracked, 2^-32 events dropped), consistent with all measurements, refereed by nobody; conjectures, not results.

weakkey-R4 edit-model R=4 'effects' (z = -31 at 2^16 with 7 conditions, nominal density 2^-224; z = -219.5 with 16 conditions, 2^-512): the round-3/4 conditions were imposed by editing the state, never realized as keys; the densities are nominal under an independence assumption; the classes are far below 2^-64. Not a finding; kept only as a hint for next step 3.

weakkey-R3 uniform-state classes (2^-160, 2^-192): confirmed exactly as stated by the referee, but the model is a long-message heuristic and the key-model probe showed the class is NOT realizable with real keys for the base message (A3 pins the H3 knob bytes). Usable as trail anatomy, not as a weak-key result; the exact-key classes (2^-32, 2^-64, 2^-96) are the ones in the margin table.

hillclimb-R4's span objective results (mspan 583.5 vs null 609.8 at the round-4 entry; the 48 B lane-1-byte-0 family): internal-state quantities an attacker cannot observe; the output statistics of every winner are null (2 x 2^30, 2 x 2^28, 7 x 2^26). Not an effect.

Single-lens, not independently reproduced (not refuted; candidates for the cheap re-checks in the next steps, but not results): bias-R1's exact R=1 statement that w0 ^= 2^63 leaves output bits 0..6 unchanged (2^31 keys); cube-R4's R=1 near-neutrality (violations at 2^-9.7); cube-R2's R=2 circular-interval statement (24 keys) and constant top bits (3 keys); hillclimb-R1's 48 B results (R=1 remainder byte 12 bit 0 at 2^-9.86; R=2 sign determinism of the additive difference, z = +8091 at 2^26; byte 45 = 0x08 bias) and hillclimb-R2's 48 B c24 excess; the 61 B / 63 B R=2 collision counts (18/2^24, 26/2^24) themselves (the family's length-independence is supported by the reproduced 29 B and 64 B runs); smt-R1's pair A (lane 2 ^ 0x1000007900000000, lane 3 ^ 1, R=1 rate 2^-0.31); weakkey-R1's B0 x lane 0 + 2^48 (R=3 |z| = 144 at 2^24) and B2 x lane 2 + 2^56 (R=2 conditional 2^-19.83); weakkey-R4's B2 x lane 2 + 2^32 R=3 conditional bias (z = -352 at 2^26); the lane-3 += 8 pair's R=2 collisions (36 in 2^27+2^25, found by a repro agent, not re-reproduced). The two-lens R=2 biases w3 ^ 2^31 (eps -2^-6.1; bias-R1 z = -1333 at 2^31, bias-R2 z = -1884.5 at 2^32) and w0 ^ 2^63 (bit 62; z = -18.4 at 2^31 and -10.6 at 2^28.75) agree with each other but were not on the reproduction list; listed in the table as two-lens, not as verified.

SMT time-outs (every R >= 2 query with >= 13 bits of difference freedom, every multi-key K >= 2 query at R >= 2, the R=4 'existence' query): no evidence for or against anything; the per-fixed-key UNSAT and brute-force facts (no single-bit / single-byte / lane-3 additive difference below 2^24 collides at R = 2, 3, 4 under key0 and key1) are what an ideal function would show and are not effects. smt-R1's key-specific SAT pairs (density 2^-256) are not effects either.

cube-R4's e192 entry as written: the listed m2_hex flips byte 16 (lane 2 bit 0), a transcription error; the referee found the intended byte-24 pair reproduces the fixed-key cube exactly (z = -10.9, -34.3, +73.7, -33.5) and the literal pair shows nothing. The corrected fact is kept (verified effect 10); the printed pair is discarded.

The previous panel's summary line 'about two rounds of margin against plain differentials' and hillclimb-R1's 'the 298 colliding keys have no structure': superseded. The margin is one round against distinguishers (R=3 is broken) and two against full collisions (R=2 collides at 2^-19.7, R=3 does not), and the R=2 colliding keys are explained by six byte conditions after round 1 (89 of 100).

All 'trials_log2 = 256' entries (z3 proofs) and the R=1 K=4 lane-2 bit-56 SAT pair (checked on four hard-coded keys only): not sampled rates; the proofs are listed under proven statements, the four-key pair is discarded as a rate claim.

Anything at R=4 with |z| between 3.5 and 5 in a single run (S2#1 xor bit 13 z = 4.2 at 2^26 -> 1.1 at 2^28; the S1b29p1 lo16 count z = -3.22 at 2^32 -> -0.34 on a fresh 2^30 stream; the zero-base ADD mask 0x8e80 z = 5.0 among 4 x 65535 masks): selection noise, each failed replication.

results.method: Evolutionary (mu+lambda) hill-climb over message pairs (m, m2) with the difference confined to the last packet (32 B) or the 16 remainder bytes (48 B), base bytes mutable; each candidate scored on 2^14 random keys with common random numbers per generation (key set renewed every 64 iterations, population re-scored). Objectives: 'coll' = sum over 64 output bits of log2 P(xor-difference bit = 0) (+4 log2(1+coll64) + log2(1+coll24)); 'bias' = max |z| over the 64 xor- and 64 additive-difference bits. Mutations: single-bit flips of m2 or of both, +/- small additive deltas on 32-bit halves, random bytes, difference sparsification, difference moves (lane swap, byte rotation, bit shift), fresh base, two crossovers, additive lane difference, single-bit restart. Runs: 32 B R=2 coll (1000 s, 215423 evals), 32 B R=3 bias (1000 s, 173144 evals), 48 B R=1 coll (350 s, 47516 evals), 48 B R=2 coll (650 s, 122310 evals), 3 x 48 B R=3 bias (150 s, ~42.5k evals each), plus 5 s / 40 s R=1 smoke runs. Distinct-difference hall-of-fame winners re-measured out-of-sample at 2^26 (12 pairs) and 2^28 (2 pairs) with 3 threads, reporting rounds 0..4: coll64/32/24/16, mean HW, per-bit z for xor and additive differences; keys colliding at R=2 dumped and inspected. hh_r.c copy reproduces all published vectors at R=4 (hh_test).
results.summary: The hill-climb rediscovers from random single-bit starts exactly the three single-byte structures of the earlier panel and nothing better; the base message is irrelevant (four A variants and three B variants agree within noise). Largest R with a measurable effect: R=3, output xor bit 63 of the pair B_1 (32 B, byte 29 = lane 3 bit 40) is equal with probability 0.579, |z| = 2585 at 2^28 keys (7 bits with |z| >= 6). R=2: full collisions at rate 2^-19.8 (298 / 2^28) for the byte-24 (lane 3 bits 0,1) pair A_1, with xor bits 48-63 almost never differing; the 298 colliding keys show no structure (generic cancellation, not a weak-key subspace). At 48 B (remainder path, lane 3 byte 0 not addressable) the best is R=1 collisions at 2^-9.9 (remainder byte 12 bit 0) and, at R=2, a deterministic sign of the additive output difference (add bits 57-63 set for 99.4% of keys, z = +8091 at 2^26) with 0 collisions; 48 B at R=3 shows nothing at 2^26. R=4: 0 collisions and |z| <= 3.3 in every measurement (2 x 2^28 + 15 x 2^26 keys).

best_pairs.notes: byte 29 = 0x01 (lane 3 bit 40). Output xor bit 63 equal with P=0.579 (z=-2585 at 2^28; bits 57-62: -18.5,-66.7,-158,-333,-673,-1292); no additive-difference bias. 0 full collisions in 2^28; R=2 for the same pair: coll24=4099 (ideal 16), meanHW 24.75, max|z| 16597; R=4: max|z| 2.9, 0 collisions. Additive variant byte 29 = 0x1f (B_3) gives the same 1295 at 2^26. File measure_B_1_k28.txt.

byte 24: f2->f1 (xor 0x03 = lane 3 bits 0,1). 298/2^28 full collisions (77/2^26 with another seed); coll32 253089, coll24 383180, meanHW 20.28. Xor bits 48-63 almost never differ (z -582 .. -16377), bits 1-7 rarely, bits 8-15 and 32-47 uniform, 16-31 partially equal; 77 bits with |z|>=6. The 298 colliding keys (dump_A1_R2_k28.txt) have no zero halves / no byte structure. Single-bit 0x01 and 0x07 variants: 70,79,83 per 2^26. R=3 and R=4 for this pair: 0 collisions, max|z| 3.7 / 2.5.
Same pair at R=1: collision rate 0.9962 (lane 3 byte 0 is one of the three R=1-clean bytes; failures are carries out of the byte). Found by the search within 5 s from random starts (t_r1.txt).

48 B = one packet + 16-byte remainder (UpdateRemainder s=16: v0 += (16<<32)+16, v1 halves rotated by 16, packet = bytes 0-15, lane 2 = 0, lane 3 hi = bytes 12-15 duplicated). Difference byte 44 bit 0 = remainder byte 12 bit 0 = lane 1 bit 32 and lane 3 bit 32 simultaneously. Best R=1 pair at 48 B after 350 s (47516 evals); meanHW 11.1, coll32 256913.

Same 48 B pair at R=2: additive difference out(m)-out(m2) has bits 57-63 set for ~99.4% of keys (z = +8020..+8091), i.e. out(m2)-out(m) in (0, 2^57] with a deterministic sign; xor bits 49-55 and 57-63 also biased (21 bits with |z|>=6); 0 full collisions, coll24 = 6 (ideal 4), meanHW 29.4. R=3/R=4: max|z| 3.3 / 3.3, nothing.

Best 48 B R=2 pair of the collision-objective search (650 s, 122310 evals): byte 45 = 0x08 (remainder byte 13 bit 3 = lane 1 bit 43 = lane 3 bit 43). Xor bit 63 equal with P ~ 0.95 (z=-7402), 22 bits with |z|>=6, coll24 = 14 (ideal 4), coll16 = 5962 (ideal 1024), meanHW 28.2; 0 full collisions at R=1 and R=2; R=3/R=4 max|z| 2.7 / 3.0.

Full search reproduction: see README.md 'Commands' (search runs are wall-clock bounded, so the evaluation counts vary; the winners do not).
results.caveats: The 'maxz' printed on the measure summary lines includes a 0.001*sum|z| tie-break term (e.g. 2590.3 vs the true bit-63 z = -2585.1; 16838 vs 16377); the per-bit z lists in the same files are exact and the values reported here are taken from them. Search-phase scores are at 2^14 keys and are in-sample; all headline numbers come from separate seeds at 2^26/2^28. Search runs are wall-clock bounded on a heavily loaded shared machine (load average 170-270), so re-running gives different evaluation counts; every run converged to its winner within the first ~60 s and did not change afterwards. The collision proxy assumes bit independence; a difference class whose advantage appears only above 2^14 keys per candidate would be invisible to it. Only lengths 32 and 48 were searched; only differences in the last packet/remainder; nothing was run at R=4 beyond re-measuring the winners (0 collisions, |z| <= 3.3, sensitivity |bias| >= 1.8e-4 at 2^28). No proof of anything; the R=2 'generic cancellation' claim is an absence of structure in 298 keys, not an algebraic statement.
results.ideas_for_next_round: (1) The search saturates on the three R=1-clean bytes; a next round should exclude them (or fix the difference) and optimise only over a differential *characteristic* through round 2, e.g. condition on intermediate state (lane-3 v1/mul0 bytes 4,6,7 being difference-free after round 1) and measure the conditional R=2/R=3 rates and the density of that key subspace -- the dump tool (--dump R) already logs colliding keys and states. (2) Use the R=2 z-profile (xor bits 48-63 never differ, 8-15/32-47 uniform) as the objective: search for a second difference that cancels the uniform 24 bits (two-block / 64 B messages with a correcting difference in the second packet were not tried here). (3) At 48 B the deterministic sign of the additive output difference at R=2 (z=+8091) is a clean distinguisher; check whether it survives to R=3 with 2^30+ keys and whether other remainder lengths (s = 20..31, where lane 3 hi duplicates lane 2 bytes) give R=1-clean positions. (4) Replace the bit-independence proxy by the actual coll32/coll24 counts at 2^18+ keys per candidate on a quieter machine. (5) Verify algebraically the R=1 rate-1 statement (failure iff a carry leaves byte 0 of v1[3], byte 6 of v0[3] or byte 4 of v1[2]) on 2^16+ keys -- cheap and would make the R=1 result an exact fact.

results.method: Analytic cancellation in the final lane-0 sum v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0] at R=1. Derived on paper (README section 1): (a) a mul word can never carry a key-independent additive difference after a product-XOR (would need P1^P2 = 2^63, impossible for 32x32-bit products), so any cancellation must be v0[0] against v1[0] with both mul words equal, which forces the lane-0 v0/v1 words and q[0] to be clean at the start of the last round; (b) the complete budget of differences the last round's two ZipperMerge additions can deliver from lane 1 into the sum: out2-out1 = d4*(2^8+2^40) + (d6+d0)*2^32 + d7*2^48 + d1*2^8 (d_k = byte differences of lane 1's v1 after step A); (c) traced backwards through Permute/swap32 and the message-step ZipperMerge to last-packet bytes that avoid every lane-0/1 multiply: lane 3 byte 2 (+delta) and lane 3 byte 1 (-delta) deliver +delta*2^32 to v0[0] and -delta*2^32 to v1[0]. Carry-event accounting gives Pr[collision] = (1-delta/256)^6 (carries inside v0[3] are harmless because they survive swap32 and the addition exactly). Tested every derived pair at 2^26 keys (3 threads, xoshiro256** keys), with R=0 sanity pairs (lane-1 analogue, predicted (255/256)^4), single-byte controls, a random base, 31/63/64-byte lengths, a 4-byte family-(ii) pattern, and an exhaustive sweep of all 1984 two-byte +-1 patterns of the last packet at 2^16 keys. Per-collision tally of which lane-0 words differ confirms the mechanism.
results.summary: R=1 collision at rate 0.9768 (65,550,593 / 67,108,863 keys) for the 32-byte pair m1 = 0^25 01 0^6, m2 = 0^26 01 0^5 (packet lane 3 += 0xFF00): each byte alone shifts the output by exactly +-2^32 (0 collisions, controls), together the shifts cancel between v0[0] and v1[0] while both mul words stay equal (100% of collisions are of this type). Rate matches the derived (255/256)^6 = 0.97683 and the six predicted failure residuals each appear ~2^26/256 times; delta=2 gives 0.95399 vs (254/256)^6 = 0.95406; same rate for a random base, 31 B, 63 B and 64 B (last packet). R=0 sanity: lane-1 analogue collides at 0.984445 vs predicted (255/256)^4 = 0.984436. A 4-byte pattern using the 2^40 cross term collides at 2^-6.02. Exhaustive +-1 two-byte sweep: bytes 25/26 opposite-sign is the only two-byte cancellation not built from the three known clean bytes. Largest R with a measurable effect: R=2 (headline pair: 0 collisions but 14 output bits with |z|>=6, max |z|=7966 at 2^26; reference lane-3-byte-0 pair: 100/2^26 = 2^-19.4 collisions, all of which are v0/v1 sum cancellations with equal mul words, i.e. the chance version of the same mechanism). R=3, R=4: 0 collisions and no bit with |z|>=6 (max 3.7) for every pair. Structural argument (conjecture) that at R>=2 every path into the cancellation budget passes a polluted multiply, so no designed pattern beats ~2^-19 at R=2.

best_pairs.notes: Packet lane 3 += 0xFF00 (byte 26 += 1, byte 25 -= 1). Predicted (255/256)^6 = 0.97683, measured 0.97678. All 65,550,593 collisions have v0[0] and v1[0] differing (+2^32 / -2^32) with mul0[0], mul1[0] equal. Failures = six carry events, residual out2-out1 values -2^32+2^8 (259,011), 2^40-2^48 (256,312), +2^24 (255,775), 2^48-2^40-2^24 (255,285), 2^48-2^8 (255,198), 2^8+2^40-2^48. Same rate on a random base (0.97676), 31 B (0.97678), 63 B (0.97677). R=2: 0 collisions but 14 bits with |z|>=6 (max 7966 at bit 62). R=3/4: nothing (|z|<=3.2).

Same difference in the last packet of a 64-byte message (bytes 57/58): 0.976767, showing the effect is independent of the preceding packet and of the public initial mul constants. R=2: 14 biased bits (max |z| 7897), R=3/4 nothing.

R=0 sanity check of the same algebra: packet lane 1 += 2^48-1 (byte 14 += 1, byte 8 -= 1) cancels inside the message Update; predicted (255/256)^4 = 0.984436, measured 0.984445; residuals +2^24, 2^48-2^8, 2^40-2^48, 2^48-2^40-2^24 at ~258K each. Byte 14 alone: 0 collisions, out2-out1 = +2^32 for 99.22% of keys (predicted (255/256)^2). At R=1 this pair gives 0 collisions (the -2^32 lands in hi32(v1[0]) and hits mul1[0]) but 27 output bits with |z|>=6.

Family (ii): lane 3 byte 3 +1, lane 2 byte 6 -1, lane 3 bytes 1 and 2 -128; cancellation (2^8+2^40) - 2^8 - 128*2^32 - 128*2^32 = 0 mod 2^64 using the 2^40 cross term. Rate 2^-6.02 (the +-128 bytes carry with probability 1/2 at each checkpoint). All collisions are v0/v1 sum cancellations. R=2..4: nothing.

Reference pair from the previous panel (lane 3 byte 0 += 1), re-measured: R=1 0.996037 with all four lane-0 words equal (state collision, not sum cancellation); R=2 100/2^26 collisions and ALL 100 are v0[0]/v1[0] sum cancellations with equal mul words, i.e. the chance event d4 = 0, d6 = -d0 of the budget formula on the bytes polluted by mul0'[3]; 39 bits with |z|>=6 at R=2. R=3/4: nothing. Not a new pair; listed because it pins down the R=2 mechanism.

Headline pair at R=2: 0 collisions in 2^26 keys, but 14 output-difference bits with |z|>=6 (max |z| = 7965.6 at bit 62): the additive output difference is confined to |out2-out1| < ~2^57 because the round-2 lane-0 product differences are (24-bit)x(32-bit). Weaker than a single byte at R=2 (lane 3 byte 1 alone: 15 bits; lane 3 byte 0: 39 bits).

results.caveats: (1) All rates use one key stream (xoshiro256** seeded from salt 1, 3 threads x 22,369,621 = 67,108,863 keys); no second seed was run, but every measured rate agrees with its closed-form prediction to 1e-4 and the R=0 sanity pairs match to 1e-5. (2) The closed forms (1-delta/256)^6 and (255/256)^4 neglect O(2^-16) events (carry out of a 32-bit half) and treat the carry checkpoints as independent uniform bytes. (3) The statement that at R>=2 no designed pattern can beat the chance cancellation ~2^-19 is a structural argument (every path from the last packet into the cancellation budget passes one polluted multiply) supported by the measurements, not a proof; it was not searched beyond the +-1 two-byte sweep (2^16 keys per cell, R=1 and R=2 only) and the 12 designed pairs. (4) The R=2 bias of the headline pair (14 bits, |z| up to 7966) is a distinguisher, not a collision; it is weaker than the single-byte lane-3 differences already known. (5) Nothing at R=3 or R=4 in 2^26 keys per pair (max |z| 3.7); no claim about the published hash beyond that. (6) Differences were placed only in the last packet; differences confined to lanes 0/1 of the last packet were analysed on paper (cost >= ~2^-17 at R=1 because they pollute a lane-1 multiply) but only the lane-1 R=0 sanity pair was measured. (7) The random-base pair was first run with m1 == m2 by mistake; the reported run_log2_26.txt is the corrected rerun (m2 differs in bytes 25/26).
results.ideas_for_next_round: (a) Turn section 1.1 + 1.2 into a checked statement for R=2: enumerate all last-packet byte differences, taint them through two rounds with the rule "every 32-bit half of v0/v1 is an operand of exactly one multiply", and verify by enumeration that every path into the lane-0 cancellation budget crosses a polluted multiply; this would make the R>=2 claim a computed fact. (b) At R=2 the only surviving mechanism is the chance cancellation d4 = 0, d6 = -d0 on the bytes of v1p3 polluted by mul0'[3] = init0[3] ^ (X*H + delta*H) with X, H uniform; try lane-3 low-half differences delta with special multiplicative structure (delta = 2^k-1, 2^k+1, values making delta*H's byte 3 vanish more often) at 2^28 keys to see whether the 2^-16 factor moves at all; my analysis says it cannot, a measurement would settle it. (c) Apply the same additive-budget method to Finalize128 (outputs v0[0]+mul0[0]+v1[2]+mul1[2] and v0[1]+mul0[1]+v1[3]+mul1[3]): cross-lane sums give a larger budget with more cancellation freedom, and 6 rounds may still leave the last round analysable. (d) Two-packet differences: put a difference in the second-to-last packet whose lane-2/3 image in v0''[2], v0''[3] is cancelled by the last packet using the same byte-routing tables (the budget formula applies to v0''[3] bytes 2/4 directly), which might buy one extra round. (e) Conditional-key experiments on the 2^-32 zero-co-operand events (lo32(v0p0) = 0) to confirm the only multiply-passing cancellation and its exact density. (f) A closed-form proof that (255/256)^6 is exact up to 2^-16 by enumerating the carry events symbolically (the six residual differences are already identified with counts).

results.method: Exact QF_BV model of HighwayHash-64 (Reset + Update(one 32-byte packet) + R PermuteAndUpdate rounds + lane-0 sum) in z3 4.15.4: 64-bit lanes, 32x32->64 multiplies as ZeroExt+BVMul, ZipperMerge as Extract/Concat byte permutation. Validated: R=4 reproduces kExpected64[32] (a0c964d9ecd580fc, kTestKey1, data 00..1f) and the 64-byte two-packet value, and agrees with the reduced-round C (hh_r.c, which passes all 65 published vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4) on 20 random (key,packet) cases at R=0..4. Queries: (1) R=0 proof with symbolic key and packet; (2) R=1 existence with symbolic key; (3) multi-key: K=1..4 hard-coded random keys (random.Random(2026)), base message fixed, XOR difference free in lanes 2,3 / single bit / lanes 0,1 / all lanes, at R=1 and R=2; (4) UNSAT attempts (2 keys, lane-0 bit-63 flip with only p0 free; single-bit differences at R=2 for one key; symbolic-key non-collision and implication proofs). Every SAT model was re-checked with the C code and measured over 2^20 then 2^24 random keys (splitmix64 key stream) with per-bit z-scores of the output XOR difference.
results.summary: Computed facts: (a) R=0: z3 proves (UNSAT in 0.03 s, symbolic key and packet) that any difference confined to lane 3, or to lanes 2+3, of the last packet collides for every key. (b) R=1 existence with a symbolic key is SAT in 33.5 s (key-specific pair, 0/2^20 random keys). (c) R=1 multi-key with K=4 fixed keys: the single-bit query returns lane-3 bit 0 in 0.1 s (rate 2^-0.01 over 2^24 keys = the previous panel's known best) and the free lanes-2,3 query returns a NEW multi-bit pair (lane2 ^ 0x1000007900000000, lane3 ^ 1) in 94 s with rate 2^-0.31 over 2^24 keys. (d) R=2: the lane-3 bit-0 pair gives 15 collisions in 2^24 keys (2^-20.1) and output-XOR bit 63 is fixed (z = -4094 at 2^24; 39 bits with |z| >= 6), so R=2 is the largest R with a measurable effect here; the multi-key SMT searches at R=2 (K=1,2, difference in lanes 2,3) hit their 240/360 s time-boxes without a model, and z3 proves in 4.3 s that no single-bit difference of the base message collides at R=2 for key 1. (e) R=3: 0/2^22 and max |z| 2.1 for both SMT pairs. (f) UNSAT attempt: 'lane-0 bit 63 flip, only p0 free, 2 keys, R=1' is UNSAT in 0.8 s (consistent with the prior sweep's deterministic output bit); symbolic-key non-collision/implication proofs at R=1,2 time out at 90-150 s. No R=3 or R=4 effect was found.

best_pairs.notes: Pair B = lane 3 bit 0 flip (byte 24 of the packet). Found by z3 in 0.1 s as the K=4 single-bit multi-key model at R=1 (q2_R1_K4_dbit); identical to the previous panel's best family. At R=2: 15 collisions / 2^24 keys (seed 7) and output-XOR bit 63 has z=-4094 (always 1), 39 of 64 bits |z|>=6. R=3: 0/2^22, max|z| 2.1.
Same pair B at R=1: 16710137/2^24 collisions (seed 7); collides for all 4 hard-coded solver keys (C-checked).

Pair A, new: z3 model of q2_R1_K4_dl23 (K=4 fixed keys, base fixed, XOR difference free in lanes 2,3), 94 s. XOR difference lane2 = 0x1000007900000000 (bits 32,35,36,37,38,60), lane3 = 0x1. 13575747/2^24 collisions at R=1 (seed 7); R=2: 0/2^24, max|z| 2.1; R=3: 0/2^22.

results.caveats: Shared machine: each z3 process got ~50-80% of a core, so the time-boxes (wall-clock) correspond to less CPU; 'unknown' means the box expired, not that the query is hard in principle. The R=2 K=2 lanes-2,3 query was killed at the overall 40-minute budget before its 360 s box ended. Pair B (lane 3 bit 0) is not new: it is the previous panel's best R=1/R=2 family; the SMT contribution is that the K=4 multi-key single-bit model finds it in 0.1 s and the free lanes-2,3 model finds a different multi-bit pair (A) at rate 2^-0.31. The R=0 result is a formal proof (UNSAT with symbolic key and packet); the R=1 conditional implication (lane-2 bit-63 path) and the symbolic-key non-collision statements for lane-0/1 bit 63 at R=1,2 did NOT finish (unknown at 90-150 s), so they remain conjecture. 'q4_unsat' (UNSAT 0.8 s) is for two specific keys with only p0 free, not a statement over all keys. Multi-key models with the base message free (first batch, p1.log/p2.log) all timed out; the reported SAT models use the fixed base message 09f1fd9d03f0a9b4 e4a7e10bb6c9d6e5 5d5bca4696b343b3 70d29b6c7d22528d. z-scores are for the XOR of the two outputs over the key stream splitmix64(seed) (seed 1 for 2^20, seed 7 for 2^24/2^22); 'trials_log2=256' for the R=0 entry denotes the proof over all keys, not sampling. Nothing was found at R=3 (0/2^22, |z|<=2.1) or R=4 (not run here; prior panel 0/2^32).
results.ideas_for_next_round: 1) R=2 is the frontier: pair B leaves output-XOR bit 63 fixed (z=-4094 at 2^24) and 39 biased bits; run the K=4 multi-key SMT at R=2 seeded with lane-3 bit 0 plus a free compensating difference in lanes 0,1 (or lane 3 byte 5, which the prior panel found biased at R=3) and with the base message free, on the x86 bench host with hours instead of minutes. 2) Replace the value-level model by a signed-difference (carry-condition) model: encode the two executions as value + difference with explicit carry bits, which is what made pair B solvable in 0.1 s; export via z3's bit-blast tactic to a .cnf and run kissat/CaDiCaL (z3's internal SAT is the bottleneck for the 32x32 multipliers). 3) Symbolic-key proofs become tractable if key lanes 0,1 are fixed and only key lanes 2,3 are symbolic (all sym x sym multiplies then sit in unused words at R=1): prove the exact conditional collision statement for lane-2 bit 63 / lane-3 bit 0 and measure P(condition) directly. 4) For the UNSAT lane, restrict to one key and single-bit differences at R=3 (256 candidates, each a constant-difference propagation): a fast UNSAT would be an exact per-key non-collision statement at R=3. 5) Try the R=2 K=1..4 searches with base free but difference restricted to the 3 'R=1-clean' bytes (lane 2 bytes 4,7, lane 3 byte 0) so the round-1 state difference is tiny and the solver only has to control round-2 carries.

results.method: Weak-key conditioning at reduced rounds: single 32-byte packet, so the packet Update's zero-co-operand conditions are linear in the key and keys are sampled directly from the subspace. A<i>: hi32(key[i]) = hi32(init0[i]) silences mul0[i] (lo32 difference in lane i passes); B<i>: lo32(key[i]) = lo32(init0[i]) ^ (-lo32(init1[i]) mod 2^32) silences mul1[i] (hi32 difference passes). Driver wk1.cpp (copy of the reference C with round-configurable finalization from the previous panel; reproduces all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4) absorbs both messages per key and records at R=0..4: full 64-bit collisions, per-output-bit XOR bias z, mean HW, per-state-word equality. Sweep: 9 condition sets (none, A0-A3, B0-B3) x 256 additive single-bit differences (+2^k on lane L) x 2^20 keys; then 2^28 conditional keys on the best cell, 2^26 unconditional baseline, seven exact two-condition subspaces (A3+X, density 2^-64) at 2^22, precision runs (2^24-2^26) on the B0/B2/L3-byte-5 cells, and a trail diagnostic (trail.cpp) tallying which state words/bytes differ after the packet step and each round.
results.summary: Largest R with a measurable effect stays R=3, but weak-key class A3 (hi32(key[3]) = 0x243f6a88, density 2^-32) adds a new R=3 distinguisher for the simplest difference (+1 in lane 3 of the last packet): output bit 63 of the two hashes agrees with probability 0.566 (z = -2169 at 2^28 conditional keys; bits 58-63 all |z| >= 38), absent unconditionally (|z| = 2.4 at 2^26). At R=2 the same class raises the collision rate from 2^-19.6 (83/2^26) to 2^-9.86 (289289/2^28); mechanism verified by the trail diagnostic (A3 keeps mul0[3] clean at the packet step; the R=2 collision is the round-1 lane-1 pollution staying out of the ZipperMerge bytes that cross into lane 0). R=3 collisions: 0 in 2^28 conditional keys, so the class contributes < 2^-58 unconditionally; at R=2 the class is irrelevant since 2^-32 x 2^-9.86 << 2^-19.6. B2 + L2:+2^56 gives R=2 collisions at 2^-19.83 (0 unconditionally); B0 + L0:+2^48 gives an R=3 bias |z| = 144 at 2^24. No second packet-step condition changes R=2/R=3 (except A3+A1, which kills the R=2 event). R=4: 0 collisions and max |z| < 6 in all 9 x 256 x 64 bit tests at 2^20 and max |z| = 2.6 at 2^28 on the best conditional cell: the published function keeps >= 1 round of margin inside the weak-key subspaces.

results.caveats: Single 32-byte packet only (the only length where the zero-co-operand conditions are linear in the key); for longer messages the analogous conditions are nonlinear state conditions before the last packet with the same heuristic density, not sampled here. Only packet-step conditions were sampled; in-round (state) conditions of round 1 were analysed by hand (they cost 2^-32 each and for the lane-3-byte-0 difference the lane-3 multiply of round 1 cannot be silenced by any key choice because hi32(v0[3]) itself carries the difference) but not sampled, so the 'R=3 trail cost >= 2^-64' statement is a conjecture. 'No effect at R=4' is bounded by the sample sizes (2^20 per sweep cell: |z| sensitivity ~2^-10, collision floor 2^-20; 2^28 on the single best conditional cell: |z| sensitivity 2^-14). Base message fixed (splitmix 0x5EED lanes); carries make rates base-dependent at the few-percent level. The weak-key R=2 gain does not translate into an unconditional effect (2^-32 x 2^-9.86 << 2^-19.6).
results.ideas_for_next_round: 1. Sample the round-1 state conditions exactly: under B<i> the condition lo32(v0[i]) == 0 at round 1 reduces to 4 bytes of the post-packet v1 words (v1[2] bytes 2,3 <- hi32(key[2]) bytes 2,3; v1[3] byte 4 <- lo32(key[3]) byte 0; v1[2] byte 5 <- the attacker's choice of p[2] hi32), so B2 + C2 (density 2^-56 with a chosen message) is constructible byte by byte; measure whether it moves the L2:+2^56 / L3:+1 trails to R=3. 2. Search for a last-packet difference whose round-1 pollution is confined to multiplies of the 'easy' type (hi32(v1) differences needing lo32(v0)==0), e.g. two-lane cancelling differences (L3:+1 with L2:-2^32 cancels v1[2]); the sweep only covered single +2^k. 3. Exploit the R=3 bias (bit 63 agrees with p = 0.566 under A3) as a key-class test: with 2^12 chosen-message pairs per key one can decide membership in the 2^-32 class, i.e. a 32-bit key leak at R=3; check whether any residue survives at R=4 with 2^32+ keys on the A3 cell (needs ~1 CPU-hour). 4. Longer messages: sample the state before the last packet uniformly (random-state model) with the same conditions to see whether the public mul0/mul1 constants matter. 5. Prove the R=1 near-deterministic collisions and the R=2 2^-10 event exactly (carry-free byte-routing argument plus the (x*h)^((x+2^16)*h) confinement probability).

results.method: High-sample per-bit bias distinguisher on round-reduced HighwayHash-64 (32-byte messages, difference in the only packet, keys = 4 uniform 64-bit words from xoshiro256**). One Reset per key, then Update(packet)+R rounds for the base message and each alternate; per (R, pair) 64 bit-counters of D_xor = H(m1)^H(m2) and 64 of D_sub = H(m1)-H(m2) mod 2^64 (bit-sliced carry-save counters), plus low-16/low-32/full collision counts; z_b = (c_b - N/2)/sqrt(N/4). Run A: the six assigned pairs (~w3, w0+2^32, w3^bit31, w0^bit63, ~w2~w3, random control) at R=1,2, N = 2^31 keys (8 chunks x 2^28, seed 1; stopped at 2^31 to fund run B). Run B: the strongest R=3 cells of the earlier 2^20 single-bit sweep (w3^bit40, w3^bit41) plus the R=2-colliding w3^bit0, at R=2,3,4, N = 2^32 keys (16 chunks x 2^28, seed 2). Plus exact_check.cpp for an algebraic R=1 statement over 8 further base messages. The modified C (hh_r.c) reproduces all 65 kExpected64 vectors and the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4 (./hh_test), and a self-check asserts the per-key path equals HighwayHash64Rounds(.,r) and HighwayHash64 before each run.
results.summary: Largest R with a measurable effect is R=3 (one round short of the published function): flipping bit 40 (or 41) of w3 biases output-difference bit 63 by -0.0766 (|z| = 10040 at 2^32 keys; bits 56..62 biased too, halving per bit), and w3^bit0 leaves a marginal trace (bit 63 z = -8.7 / +7.2). At R=2, w3^bit0 gives full 64-bit collisions at rate 2^-19.71 (4998 in 2^32 keys), low-32-bit collisions at 2^-10.05 and 24 output bits (0..7, 48..63) essentially fixed; w3^bit40 gives low-16-bit collisions for 38.6% of keys; w3^bit31 biases bit 63 by 2^-6.1 (z=-1333 at 2^31); w0^bit63 biases bit 62 by 2^-12.3 (z=-18.4). The complements ~w3, ~w2~w3, the additive w0+2^32 and the random control are at the noise floor at R=2 (|bias| < 2^-13.9). At R=1: exact statement, w0^bit63 leaves the low 7 output bits unchanged for every key (2^31 + 2^21 keys, 0 exceptions, derivation in README), low-16 collisions for 50.001% of keys, low-32 for 2^-10.0; w0+2^32 has bias 2^-10.4 on bit 55 (z=68). R=4 (published): nothing at 2^32 keys for the three strongest R=3 differentials, max |z| = 3.03 over 9 cells x 128 statistics, i.e. every bit of D_xor and D_sub has |bias| < 4.6e-5 = 2^-14.4; 0 full collisions in 3 x 2^32; low-16/32 collision counts at their ideal values.

results.caveats: Single fixed base message for the main statistics (splitmix64 seed 0x5EED words, same base as angles/structured-differences); the exact R=1 statement was additionally checked on 8 other base messages. The carry-driven bias magnitudes (R=2 and R=3 lane-3 flips) are per message pair: they depend on the base message's bits around the flipped position, though the earlier 2^20 sweep shows the same positional ordering. The six-pair run was stopped at 2^31 keys instead of the planned 2^32 (budget guard, to afford the 2^32 R=2..4 run), so its R=2 null results have sensitivity |bias| < 2^-13.9 rather than 2^-14.4. Per-bit bias tests see collision structure only above ~p_c/2, so an R=4 collision rate below ~2^-30 would be invisible to both the bias statistics and the direct counts at 2^32. Only three differentials were tested at R=3/R=4; they were chosen from a single-bit sweep, so multi-bit or additive differentials at R=3/R=4 remain unscanned. Keys were xoshiro256** streams (seeded per chunk/thread as printed), not a hardware RNG. No timing claims.
results.ideas_for_next_round: (1) The R=3 top-bit bias of w3^bit40 (2^-3.7) comes from a carry-free path through the top bits; try optimizing the base message (or a few base bits near w3 bits 32..47) and two-bit combinations (bit40+bit41, bit40 of w3 with bit 63 of w1/w0) to maximize the R=3 bias, then re-test R=4 at 2^34..2^36 keys (2^-17..2^-18 sensitivity) with the best one; the R=2->R=3 decay was 0.5 -> 2^-3.7, so a 2^-10..2^-16 residue at R=4 is not excluded. (2) Use the 1024-bit state: measure the R=3 state-word bias profile (which of v0[0],v1[0],mul0[0],mul1[0] carries the bit-63 agreement) and derive an exact conditional statement (key subspace where lo32(v0[3]) has small top bits) to obtain a conditional R=4 distinguisher with stated density. (3) For w3^bit0 at R=2 the 2^-19.7 full-collision rate is measured; characterize the colliding-key set algebraically (which 20 key bits / products must vanish) to see whether a message-side choice (other w0..w2) can raise it and whether the R=3 trace (z=-8.7) grows with a better base. (4) Longer messages with the difference in the last packet plus the R=3 pairs, and the remainder path (sizes 1..31) where v1 is rotated by size, may offer other carry-free top-bit paths.

results.method: Cube testers / algebraic-degree probes: for a chosen set of input bits (message bits of a 32-byte single packet, or key bits) and a d-cube of them (d=2..24; other inputs fixed, key = 4 uniformly random words, a fresh key per cube), all 2^d assignments are hashed with R finalization rounds; a Moebius transform over the cube yields the ANF of every output bit (and, for d<=18, of all 1024 state bits) restricted to the cube: restricted degree (the d-cube sum is the top coefficient), monomial counts per level (calibrated against C(d,k)/2), and balancedness z. 17 variable sets (lane 0/1/2/3, low/high halves, lanes 2+3, all; key[0], key[3], halves, key[2..3], all key bits), modes random/lowest/highest bits, R=0,1,2 (+R=3 controls), 776+6 jobs. Leads were then measured as rates over random keys with a pair test (fixed message pair, per-bit equality z-scores, full-collision counts, colliding keys printed) for R=0..4, and witnesses re-hashed through the public HighwayHash64Rounds path (the copy reproduces all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4).
results.summary: Largest R with a measurable effect: R=2. The cube tester shows R=1 is algebraically broken (lane-3 message bits: all 64 output bits have restricted degree <= 20 on 24-cubes, bits 0-8 degree 4-11, bit 63 degree 3; the low 32 bits of w3 leave 16 output bits constant on all 56 cubes/keys; key[3] bits: output bits 0-7 have degree <= 8 on 24-cubes; a single-bit w3 difference collides fully for 99.60% of keys). At R=2 the bulk is random-like (monomial counts match C(d,k)/2) but the lowest bits of lane 3 still leak: the fixed pair m1 = 32 zero bytes, m2 = same with byte 24 = 0x01 gives 15 full 64-bit collisions in 2^24 random keys (rate 2^-20.09; 21/2^24 with random base messages), the top 2 output bits equal for essentially all keys (z = 4094 at 2^24), top-8 bits equal at 2^-0.02, low-24 bits at 2^-9.45, 39 output bits with |z| >= 6; cubes of the low 16 bits of w3 leave output bits 60-63 constant, and output bit 0 had restricted degree 2-3 below the cube dimension in 5 of 7 random 22/24-cubes of lane-3 bits (no uniform bound). The same pair at R=3 (2^24 keys) and all specs at R=4 (2^20) are at noise (max|z| <= 3.2, 0 collisions). The published panel sweep already contained the R=2 single-bit lane-3 signal (bit0_L3 coll64=2/2^20); this run rediscovers it independently, explains it algebraically and adds 2^24 precision with verified witness keys.

results.caveats: (1) The R=2 single-bit lane-3 signal is not new in kind: the panel's sweep_bits_32B_log2_20.txt already shows bit0_L3 R=2 coll64=2, bit1_L3 coll64=2, bit4_L3 coll64=1 at 2^20; what is new is the 2^24 precision on a fixed pair, the verified witness keys, the neighbourhood map, and the algebraic-degree localisation. (2) Nothing at R=3 or R=4: the published function keeps a margin of two rounds against everything tried here; the R=2 collision rate 2^-20 says nothing about R=4. (3) Cube 'degree' numbers are restricted degrees on random affine subcubes (lower bounds on the true degree; evidence for an upper bound only where many cubes of larger dimension all vanished, as stated per cell); cubes of the largest sizes had only 1-4 cubes each and the low/high structured modes only 2 keys. (4) The R=2 'output bit 0 degree 2-3 below the cube dimension' observation held in 5 of 7 large cubes and failed in 2, so it is a non-random signature, not a degree bound; no collision use is known. (5) All messages are 32-byte single packets (differences in the only/last packet); the remainder path and multi-packet prefixes were not tested (a random first packet should behave like a random key, but this was not run). (6) The machine was heavily shared (load ~130-270 on 12 cores); no timing claims. (7) Balancedness z over a cube is for one fixed key per cube; the rates over keys come from the pair tests.
results.ideas_for_next_round: (a) Push the R=2 lead toward R=3 by choosing the difference to survive one more byte-routing step: search over multi-bit lane-3 differences (bits 0-7 plus compensating bits in lanes 2/3) with the cube tester's constant-bit map as fitness, and over 'byte-6/byte-4 of v0[3]' targeted additive differences (the +2^48 and +2^32 image of bit 0) applied directly as message differences in lanes 2/3 of an earlier packet. (b) Conditional keys: the R=2 collisions occur for ~2^-20 of keys; characterise the colliding keys (15 witnesses available) to find the key subspace (likely conditions on hi32(v0[3]) and lo32(v0[2]) making the product differences small) and its density, then test whether a message-only condition can replace it. (c) Cube attack on the key at R=1: the superpolys of output bits 0-7 in key[3] bits have degree <= 8; linearise to recover key[3] bits from chosen 32-byte messages, then check what survives at R=2 with the bit-0 (carry-free) output bit. (d) Two-packet messages: put the +2^48/+2^32 image differences in packet 0 and use packet 1 to cancel, extending the 'silent pass' by one Update. (e) Provable side: the R=1 99.6% collision has a clean byte-routing proof sketch (README); formalising 'no single-bit lane-3 difference reaches lane 0 before round 2 except through byte carries' would give an exact R=1 statement.

results.method: Evolutionary (mu+lambda, mu=lambda=14) hill-climb over message pairs (m, m2) with the difference confined to the last 32-byte packet (32 B) or the 16 remainder bytes (48 B), all base bytes mutable, scored on a DIRECT partial/near-collision objective at round R over 2^16 common random keys per generation (key set renewed every 40 generations, population + hall of fame re-scored): 8 log2(1+c64) + 3 log2(1+c32) + 3 log2(1+ch32) + 2 log2(1+c24) + log2(1+c16) + 2 log2(1+n8) + log2(1+n16) + log2(1+a8) + 0.25(proxy+64) (c* = keys with out1^out2 zero on all/low32/high32/low24/low16 bits, n8/n16 = popcount(out1^out2) <= 8/16, a8 = additive difference with <= 8 bits, proxy = sum log2 P(bit equal) as tie-breaker); alternative objective 'bias' = max |z| over 64 xor + 64 additive difference bits. Mutations: bit flips of m2 / of both, +-(1..255)<<8b on 32-bit halves or 64-bit lanes of m2 / both, random base byte, sparsify, move (lane swap / byte rotation / bit shift), fresh base, crossover, additive lane difference m +- d<<s, two-lane compensating +d/-d, sparse 1..4-bit 64-bit additive difference, random byte xor, single-bit restart. Population seeded with every known structure (A lane 3 byte 0, B lane 3 byte 5, the R=1 sum-cancellation pair, the weak-key lane 3 +1 pair; C1/C2 at 48 B) plus random single-bit starts. Runs (1 thread each, 780 s): S1 32 B R=2 pc (74900 evals x 2^16 keys), S2 48 B R=2 pc (56232), S3 32 B R=3 bias (60726). Distinct-difference hall-of-fame winners re-measured out of sample with 3 threads and fresh splitmix64 key seeds at 2^26 (S1 top 3, S3 top 2, S2 top 1) and 2^28 (S1 best, R=0..2), plus two designed pairs (lane 3 byte 0 via the remainder path at 61 B and 63 B) at 2^24, reporting per R=0..4: c64/c32/ch32/c24/c16, n8/n16/a8, mean HW, per-bit z for xor and additive differences. hh_r.c (copy from angles/structured-differences) reproduces all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4 (hh_test run this session).
results.summary: The direct partial-collision hill-climb, seeded with every known structure and equipped with multi-lane, additive and compensating mutations, never left the three single-byte families already known: at R=2 it ranks lane 3 byte 0 first (byte 24 = 0x01: 313/2^28 full collisions = 2^-19.71 out of sample; 71-88 per 2^26 for the 0x01/0x07/0x1f variants), at R=3 the bias objective stays on lane 3 byte 5 (xor output bit 63 equal with P = 0.579, |z| = 1294 at 2^26, 7 bits with |z| >= 6, 0 collisions), and at 48 B the best it finds is a two-byte difference in remainder bytes 13-14 (bytes 45,46 = 0xf0,0x07) with c24 = 28 vs ideal 4 at 2^26 and no full collisions. New facts: the R=2 family passes unchanged through the remainder path (61 B: 18/2^24 = 2^-19.83, 63 B: 26/2^24 = 2^-19.30, same meanHW 20.21 and bit-63 determinism), so it is length-independent wherever lane 3 byte 0 is addressable. R=4 (published): 0 collisions in 6 x 2^26 + 2 x 2^24 keys, largest |z| = 3.5 (noise). Largest R with a measurable effect: R=3 (bias only); full collisions above the sampling floor only up to R=2.

results.ideas_for_next_round: (1) The R=2 rate 2^-19.7 factorizes (weak-key panel) as ~2^-10 (mul0[3] pollution by hi32(v0[3]) avoided/cancelled) x 2^-9.9 (mul0[1] pollution staying out of bytes 4,6,7): an analytic model of the low-48-bit residual difference at R=2 (74 biased bits, 24 uniform) could give the exact rate and show whether any second difference (e.g. in lane 2, which enters lane 0 directly through Permute in round 2) can cancel the swap32(v0[2]) term that pollutes v1[0] in round 2; the searcher never found one, but a targeted z3/QF_BV query at R=2 with the lane-3-bit-0 difference fixed and a free lane-2 difference over 2-4 hard-coded keys would settle it faster than random mutation. (2) Run the pc-objective search unseeded at 2^18-2^20 keys per candidate (fewer evaluations, but a landscape that is not flat near single-bit differences) restricted to lanes 2-3 additive differences. (3) At 48-63 B, sweep all single-byte differences of the remainder at each s = 1..31 at 2^22 keys (31 x 31 x 256 cells is too many at 2^22; do s = 16..31 single bits at 2^20) to map where the lane-3-byte-0 family is addressable and whether any s gives a better R=2 rate. (4) For R=3 the only handle is the lane-3-byte-5 bit-63 bias (0.079); a bias search at 2^20 keys per candidate seeded with B and restricted to lane 3 hi32 additive differences would show whether multi-bit hi32 differences raise it. (5) Nothing in this or the previous panel suggests an R=4 effect; a proof attempt should target the statement that after 2 rounds every lane-0 word depends on every state word through at least one multiply with a uniformly random co-operand.

results.method: Analytic cancellation in the final lane-0 sum v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0] at R=2, derived on paper first (README section 2). (a) Both lane-0 mul words must be equal at the output (a product XOR can never carry a key-independent additive difference and never un-pollutes), so the cancellation is v0[0] against v1[0]; every 32-bit half of v0[0], v1[0] is multiplied in round 2 and every round-1 entry into lane 0 (v1'[1].b4/b6/b7 -> v0f0.b1/b4/b6, v0f1.b4/b6/b7 -> v1f0.b1/b4/b6) lands in a multiplied half, hence lane 0 must be untouched by the packet step and round 1 and q2[0] = swap32(v0f2) clean. (b) Complete round-2 budget including the new lane-1 e-terms: out2-out1 = d4(2^8+2^40) + d6 2^32 + d7 2^48 + e4 2^8 + e6 2^32 + e7 2^48 with d = byte diffs of v1'[1] = v1f1+mul0f1+swap32(v0f3), e = byte diffs of v0''[1] = v0f1+mul1f1+Z(v1')[1]; integer solutions: d4=e4=d7=e7=0, d6=-e6, or d4=-e4=+-1, d6+e6=-+256. (c) Fate table of all 32 last-packet bytes through the packet-step multiplies, ZipperMerge byte permutation, Permute and round 1: every byte except lane 3 byte 0 (message byte 24) sends a key-independent difference into a forbidden lane-0 word or a polluted mul word (mul0[2]/mul1[2]/mul1[3]) into q2[0]/q2[1]; multi-byte patterns cannot cancel because every ZipperMerge destination byte has one source. (d) For byte 24 the collision is a chance coincidence of two independent pollutions, A3 (mul0[3] packet-step product difference, footprint delta*hi32(v0[3])) and A1 (mul0[1] round-1 product difference, delta*2^16*hi32(v0''[1])): A3.b3+A1.b4=0, (A3.b2+A1.b6)+A3.b1=0, A3.b4=0 plus two carry conditions; signature v0[0].b4=+c, v1[0].b4=-c. Driver sc2.cpp (hh_r.c copy, byte-identical to sumcancel-R1's, passes all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4) absorbs both messages per key and at R=0..4 records collisions with a lane-0 word tally, additive-difference histograms, per-bit z, and after round 1 the six derived conditions (cL0, cQ0, cB4, cB7, cB1, cB60) and their coincidence with R=2 collisions; dump.cpp prints per-byte state differences of colliding keys. 20 pairs x 2^26 keys (xoshiro256**, salt 1, 3 threads): delta sweep 1,2,3,4,8,16,128,255 on byte 24, random base, 29-byte remainder-path message, three dead controls (bytes 27, 24+25, 29), six R=0 sanity pairs for the budget weights.
results.summary: No designed sum cancellation exists at R=2: the derivation shows lane 0 must be totally clean after round 1 with q2[0] clean, and tracing all 32 last-packet bytes leaves lane 3 byte 0 (message byte 24) as the only pattern whose R=2 collision probability is above the 2^-32 silencing events; its collisions are a chance coincidence of the two product pollutions A3 (mul0[3]) and A1 (mul0[1]). Measured at 2^26 keys: 100/2^26 = 2^-19.36 for delta=1 (89 on a random base, 82 in a 29-byte message), all with v0[0].b4=+c, v1[0].b4=-c and equal mul words; the six derived conditions hold for 167 keys and predict 89 of the 100 collisions; cB4 and cB60 stay at 2^-8/2^-8.6 for every delta while cQ0 falls with delta, so the count decreases monotonically (100, 52, 28, 27, 9, 4, 0, 0 for delta 1,2,3,4,8,16,128,255): delta=+-1 is the ceiling of the channel. The three patterns declared dead give 0/2^26 at R=2 (byte 29 keeps its known R=3 bias, z=-1248 at bit 63 at 2^26). R=0 checks confirm the budget weights 2^8, 2^32, 2^8+2^40, 2^48 exactly, with wrap rates 255/256, (255/256)^2, (255/256)^2, 255/256 (a wrap whose spill is not routed to lane 0 is absorbed; my a-priori (255/256)^2 for bytes 1 and 7 was corrected by the data). Nothing at R=4 (0 collisions, |z|<=3.6 over 20 pairs).

results.caveats: The impossibility statement for designed R=2 cancellation (README 2.1-2.2) is a structural trace of the reference code over key-independent differences and pollution footprints, checked by three dead controls at 2^26 and by the earlier exhaustive two-byte sweep of sumcancel-R1; it is not a proof over all 1024-bit states, and it ignores events of probability ~2^-32 (a zero key half silencing a multiply) as well as family-(ii) variants and wrap events, which is why cALL predicts 89 of 100 collisions rather than all. The headline pair B24_d1 uses the same key stream as sumcancel-R1's S3 (hence the identical count of 100); the independent measurements are the random-base (89) and 29-byte (82) pairs and the previous panel's 77-83 with other seeds. Two of my a-priori R=0 wrap-count predictions ((255/256)^2 for lane-1 bytes 1 and 7) were wrong; the data gave 255/256 and the README explains the absorption of a spill into an unrouted byte. The 2^-19.4 ceiling claim for R=2 is a conjecture supported by the fate table and the monotone delta sweep, not a computation over all 2^256 last-packet pairs. No conditional (weak-key) subspaces were run in this lane. Trial counts: 2^26 keys per pair (67,108,863 = 3 x 22,369,621), single salt.
results.ideas_for_next_round: (1) The density-2^-64 subspace {hi32(key[3]) = hi32(init0[3])} AND {hi32(v0''[1]) = 0 after the packet step} silences both pollutions A3 and A1 for the byte-24 pair, so the derivation predicts an R=2 collision rate near (1 - delta/256)^k ~ 1 there: sample it by solving the second (nonlinear in hi32(key[1]), fixed-point over the two ZipperMerge bytes) condition and check on >= 2^16 keys; it is an exact algebraic statement, not an attack (contributes 2^-64). (2) The family-(ii) solutions (d4 = -e4 = +-1, d6+e6 = -+256) and the 11 collisions outside cALL: add counters for them to see whether they explain the remaining 11 % and the 78 cALL non-collisions. (3) At R=3 the byte-29 pair leaves an exact +2^48 in v0f0 after round 1; its round-2 mul0[0] pollution is 2^16*lo32(v1'[0]) with a public XOR mask, so the R=3 bit-63 bias could be computed analytically (and maybe amplified by choosing delta with few set bits) to state the R=3 distinguisher's advantage exactly. (4) Two-packet messages where the first packet places the byte-24 difference and the second packet is chosen to cancel its lane-3 pollution are impossible by the same permutation argument, but a first-packet difference reaching lane 0 could be combined with a second-packet byte-24 difference to test whether an R=2-clean lane 0 can be produced from a dirty one (the derivation says no; a cheap sweep at 2^20 would confirm).

results.method: Exact QF_BV model of round-reduced HighwayHash-64 (Reset + Update(one 32-byte packet) + R PermuteAndUpdate rounds + lane-0 sum) written from scratch in z3 4.15.4 (64-bit lanes, 32x32->64 products as ZeroExt+BVMul, ZipperMerge as Extract/Concat byte permutation), with a pure-Python reference for constant folding and a second backend (SMT-LIB2 export -> boolector 3.2.4). New relative to smt-R1: (a) a multiplier-agnostic variant with the product replaced by an uninterpreted function MUL(lo32,hi32) so that UNSAT = 'holds for every key and every multiplier' (structural proofs), (b) boolector as a second solver, (c) additive difference families of 16/24/32 bits where the solver acts as an exhaustive prover, cross-checked by brute force, (d) every SAT model rebuilt as a hex pair, re-checked with the Python reference under each hard-coded key, and measured with a 3-thread C harness (full/top-16/top-32 collisions, per-bit z of the output XOR difference, rounds 0..R in one pass).
