results.caveats: (1) The 'largest R with an effect' by this method is 3, and only through derivative (difference) statistics; plain cube sums / restricted ANF show no low-degree output bit at R=3 or R=4 up to d=26 (a restricted degree >= d-1 on random d-subsets is evidence about the restriction only; the true degree in all 256 variables is not bounded by this test). (2) The e192 result is a fixed-key AND fixed-lane-3-word bias with key/base-dependent sign, magnitude up to ~0.07 in bits 60-63 (4 cubes; 1 of 4 cubes showed nothing); with all lanes random the per-key bias survives only in bit 63 (mean z^2 3.42 over 64 keys, 2^20 pairs each). It is weaker than the e232 bias and does not lead to a collision; no R=4 counterpart. (3) 'count' for the R=1 entry is the number of violations of the near-exact neutrality statement, not collisions; that statement is NOT exact (rate 2^-9.7). (4) The R=2 cube entries are properties of whole cubes (2^24 points) at one key / one key cube; the given m2 is just one corner. (5) The tester's R=0 output includes the packet Update only (no rounds), consistent with the panel. (6) Bases/keys come from splitmix64 with the seeds in the scripts; cube_v2 prints them and produces the identical stream as the batch binary cube (verified on seed 1013). (7) Files cube4.c, cube4, run_anf.sh, run_anf.log, run_headline.sh, run_headline.log, run_side.sh, run_side2.sh, run_side2.log, out/ and summary.txt in the directory were written by another process, not by me; they are not part of this report. (8) No timing claims; machine load 100-380.
results.ideas_for_next_round: (a) Turn the mean-z^2 (key-dependent-sign) statistic into a systematic sweep at R=3: all 256 single-bit XOR differences and all 8160 single-byte differences, K=32 keys x 2^16 pairs each, on the 'fixed key + fixed difference lane' model (vary the other three lanes): the e192 case shows over-keys averaging hides sign-varying biases, so the previous panels' R=3 maps (and the seeds' hill-climb objective, which averaged over keys) may have missed stronger conditional biases; then feed the objective 'sum over keys of z^2' to the hill-climb. (b) Condition the e192 bias on the lane-3 word: sweep w3 at a fixed key to find the words that maximise |z62| (the sign flips with w3, so some w3 should give |bias| >> 0.07), and read off the state condition (probably a carry/high-half event in lane 3's packet step or lane 1's round-1 multiply). (c) At R=4 apply the same per-key mean-z^2 test to the e232 family with n = 2^24 pairs per key and K = 16 (the R=3 bias of 0.15 in bit 63 is the input to round 4; a fourth-round residual of order 0.15 x 2^-32-ish per multiply is expected to be invisible, but a top-bit residual of ~1e-3 would show at 2^24 x 16). (d) Cube attack proper at R=2: since output bits have full restricted degree but monomial density 0.95, look for linear superpolys of small cubes in the derivative ANF (degree-1 monomials only) to recover key[3] bits from R=2 outputs; irrelevant to R=4 but a clean 'two rounds of margin' statement. (e) The R=1 near-exact neutrality (bit 63 vs lane 1, rate 2^-9.7) can be made exact by writing down the carry condition; a proof at R=1 is cheap and would bound what the first round mixes.

repros.method: Evolutionary (mu+lambda) hill-climb over message pairs (m, m2) with the difference confined to the last packet (32 B) or the 16 remainder bytes (48 B), base bytes mutable; each candidate scored on 2^14 random keys with common random numbers per generation (key set renewed every 64 iterations, population re-scored). Objectives: 'coll' = sum over 64 output bits of log2 P(xor-difference bit = 0) (+4 log2(1+coll64) + log2(1+coll24)); 'bias' = max |z| over the 64 xor- and 64 additive-difference bits. Mutations: single-bit flips of m2 or of both, +/- small additive deltas on 32-bit halves, random bytes, difference sparsification, difference moves (lane swap, byte rotation, bit shift), fresh base, two crossovers, additive lane difference, single-bit restart. Runs: 32 B R=2 coll (1000 s, 215423 evals), 32 B R=3 bias (1000 s, 173144 evals), 48 B R=1 coll (350 s, 47516 evals), 48 B R=2 coll (650 s, 122310 evals), 3 x 48 B R=3 bias (150 s, ~42.5k evals each), plus 5 s / 40 s R=1 smoke runs. Distinct-difference hall-of-fame winners re-measured out-of-sample at 2^26 (12 pairs) and 2^28 (2 pairs) with 3 threads, reporting rounds 0..4: coll64/32/24/16, mean HW, per-bit z for xor and additive differences; keys colliding at R=2 dumped and inspected. hh_r.c copy reproduces all published vectors at R=4 (hh_test).

repros.method: Analytic cancellation in the final lane-0 sum v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0] at R=1. Derived on paper (README section 1): (a) a mul word can never carry a key-independent additive difference after a product-XOR (would need P1^P2 = 2^63, impossible for 32x32-bit products), so any cancellation must be v0[0] against v1[0] with both mul words equal, which forces the lane-0 v0/v1 words and q[0] to be clean at the start of the last round; (b) the complete budget of differences the last round's two ZipperMerge additions can deliver from lane 1 into the sum: out2-out1 = d4*(2^8+2^40) + (d6+d0)*2^32 + d7*2^48 + d1*2^8 (d_k = byte differences of lane 1's v1 after step A); (c) traced backwards through Permute/swap32 and the message-step ZipperMerge to last-packet bytes that avoid every lane-0/1 multiply: lane 3 byte 2 (+delta) and lane 3 byte 1 (-delta) deliver +delta*2^32 to v0[0] and -delta*2^32 to v1[0]. Carry-event accounting gives Pr[collision] = (1-delta/256)^6 (carries inside v0[3] are harmless because they survive swap32 and the addition exactly). Tested every derived pair at 2^26 keys (3 threads, xoshiro256** keys), with R=0 sanity pairs (lane-1 analogue, predicted (255/256)^4), single-byte controls, a random base, 31/63/64-byte lengths, a 4-byte family-(ii) pattern, and an exhaustive sweep of all 1984 two-byte +-1 patterns of the last packet at 2^16 keys. Per-collision tally of which lane-0 words differ confirms the mechanism.

Derived on paper (README section 1): (a) a mul word can never carry a key-independent additive difference after a product-XOR (would need P1^P2 = 2^63, impossible for 32x32-bit products), so any cancellation must be v0[0] against v1[0] with both mul words equal, which forces the lane-0 v0/v1 words and q[0] to be clean at the start of the last round; (b) the complete budget of differences the last round's two ZipperMerge additions can deliver from lane 1 into the sum: out2-out1 = d4*(2^8+2^40) + (d6+d0)*2^32 + d7*2^48 + d1*2^8 (d_k = byte differences of lane 1's v1 after step A); (c) traced backwards through Permute/swap32 and the message-step ZipperMerge to last-packet bytes that avoid every lane-0/1 multiply: lane 3 byte 2 (+delta) and lane 3 byte 1 (-delta) deliver +delta*2^32 to v0[0] and -delta*2^32 to v1[0]. Carry-event accounting gives Pr[collision] = (1-delta/256)^6 (carries inside v0[3] are harmless because they survive swap32 and the addition exactly). Tested every derived pair at 2^26 keys (3 threads, xoshiro256** keys), with R=0 sanity pairs (lane-1 analogue, predicted (255/256)^4), single-byte controls, a random base, 31/63/64-byte lengths, a 4-byte family-(ii) pattern, and an exhaustive sweep of all 1984 two-byte +-1 patterns of the last packet at 2^16 keys. Per-collision tally of which lane-0 words differ confirms the mechanism.

Single 32-byte packet (base = splitmix64(0x5EED) lanes, as in the previous panels), so the state entering the packet Update is v0=init0^key, v1=init1^rot32(key), mul0=init0, mul1=init1. Round-1 conditions on the absorbed state S: H<i> hi32(S.v0[i])=0 (silences round-1 mul0[i]), L<i> lo32(S.v0[i]+S.mul1[i])=0 (silences round-1 mul1[i]), V<i>/W<i> hi32/lo32 of round-1 v1[i]=0. (2) A new cancellation mechanism, q-cancellation: a key-independent difference in S.v1[0] cancelled in step A of lane 0 by -swap32 of a difference in S.v0[2] before any multiply; realizable at R=1 by lane 1 byte 0 (+1) with lane 2 byte 3 (-1), and lane 1 byte 1 (+1) with lane 2 byte 1 (-1), predicted 2^-16..2^-17 (lane-1 pollution budget), single halves predicted 0. (3) R=3: pulling the last-round conditions (S2 lane 0 clean, S2.v0[2] clean, budget) back through round 2 shows all eight mul words must be clean after round 1 up to per-byte coincidences; every packet byte pollutes a mul word of its lane in the packet step and that pollution is full-width after round 1, so no designed R=3 trail exists and the cheapest confinement events are 2^-24 (lane 1) / 2^-32 (lanes 2,3; the L2 silencing of the lane-3-byte-0 channel). route3.py (byte-level K/pollution tracer) reproduces the measured S1/S2 word-equality fractions. (4) Measurable R=3 effect = top-bit bias; S3 per-word attribution shows the mechanism (narrow S2 lane 0 + the 0.153 bias of bit 63 of 32x32 products). Driver sc3.cpp on hh_r.c (byte-identical to the panel copy; ./hh_test passes all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4) records per key at r=0..4 collisions, per-bit z (xor and additive), top-16 partial collisions, word-equality fractions at S0/S1/S2, the R=2 conditions on S1, the R=3 conditions on S2 (L0,Q0,M01,M11,X467,E467,BUD,ALL3), S3 per-word bit-63/width statistics. Runs (3 threads, nice 10, xoshiro256** keys): 32 single bytes x 2^20 (salt 1); 992 two-byte patterns (all a<b, signs ++ and +-) x 2^18 brief; bytes 29 and 24 x 2^26 on a fresh stream (salt 3); q-cancel pairs + 3 controls x 2^24; family-(ii) pairs x 2^20.

Two sampling models: (1) KEY model: key uniform, round-0 conditions A<i>=H<i>@0 / B<i>=L<i>@0 as linear pins, round-1 conditions by byte-wise DFS over 4 key bytes (weakkey-R2 knob map); (2) UNIFORM-STATE model (new): the 1024-bit state S1 after the last packet is uniform (long-message heuristic), round-1 conditions set directly on S1, round-0 conditions met by BACKWARD knobs through the exact inverse packet Update (H: hi32(mul1[i]), L: lo32(v0[i]), W: lo32(v1[i]), V: hi32(v1[i]) of S1), round-2 conditions by FORWARD knobs (H: hi32(mul1[i]), L: lo32(mul1[i]) with round-1 settings re-applied, W: lo32(mul0[i]), V: hi32(mul0[i])); S0 = InvUpd(S1,packet1), message 2 absorbed from the same S0. Conditions on the entry state T of Update r: H<i>@r hi32(T.v0[i])=0 (silences mul0[i]), L<i>@r lo32(T.v0[i]+T.mul1[i])=0 (silences mul1[i]), W<i>@r lo32(T.v1[i]+T.mul0[i]+lanes[i])=0, V<i>@r hi32(same)=0. DFS takes the first solution from a random start (approximately uniform inside the class); EVERY sample is re-verified on the reference forward computation (verify_fail=0 in all reported runs). Per sample both messages absorbed, rounds applied one at a time; at R=0..4: full collisions, lane-0-words-equal, per-output-bit XOR z, mean HW, per-word AND per-byte equality of all 16 state words (the byte map is what exposes the trail). Model validation: state vs key model agree (A3: R=2 2^-9.96 vs 2^-9.99 here vs 2^-9.86 weakkey-R1; A3&H1&L2: R=2 0.973 vs 0.983 vs 0.980; R=3 bias 0.95 vs 0.97 vs 0.968 per sqrt N). New trick: the unsilenceable round-1 mul0[3] (both operands carry the difference) is made KEY-INDEPENDENT by H3@1 & W3@1 (operands 0*0 vs 1*2^16 -> constant bit-16 flip), then round-2 lane-1 multiplies silenced (H1@2, L1@2). 1 thread per run (host load average ~350), 2^10..2^18 samples.

proofs.summary: PROOF SIDE for HighwayHash-64 (R finalization rounds, R=4 published). Five lemmas with proofs (LaTeX, /…/attack/proof-trails/lemmas.tex, compiles) and numerical checks with my own traced implementation built next to the UNMODIFIED reference (the reference TU is #included; our R=4 pipeline reproduces all 65 kExpected64 vectors and the 33-byte key2 vector on every run). Proven: (1) Update_p, the round and the remainder step are permutations of the 1024-bit state (explicit inverse F^-1,E^-1,D^-1,C^-1,B^-1,A^-1 given; verified 65536/65536 on random states), so every equal-length collision is a collision of the 64-bit truncation tau=v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0] on two distinct states (fibres 2^960). (2) At R=0 the output depends only on key[0],key[1], the length and packet bytes 0..15 of each 32-byte block: any difference confined to lanes 2,3 of ANY packets collides for every key (2^20/2^20 at 32 B, 64 B first packet, 64 B both packets); corollaries: all 256 one-byte messages collide (65536/65536 keys), byte 32 of a 33-byte message and bytes 44..46 of a 47-byte message are ignored (65536/65536). The converse is NOT proven: lane-1 bytes 2,3,5 (bits 16..31, 40..47) are the carry-free part of the class (Lemma 2(iv), deterministic statement proven) and collide at R=0 with rates up to 65535/65536 (bit 17) matching the carry model (1-2^-(32-b))^2 etc. to ~1%; every lane-0 bit and the other 40 lane-1 bits: 0/65536. (3) One-step separation, exact: mul0[i] changes iff lo32(delta)!=0 and hi32(v0[i])!=0; mul1[i] changes iff the high half of v1[i] changes (always if hi32(delta) not in {0,-1}; with prob lo32(delta)/2^32 if hi32(delta)=0; 1-lo32(delta)/2^32 if hi32(delta)=-1) and lo32(v0[i]+mul1[i])!=0; for one-packet messages P[H=0]=P[L=0]=2^-32 exactly and independent (2^-64 jointly). 60 cells x 2^20 keys: 0 mismatches, all carry rates within 1 s.e.; in the conditional subspaces (density 2^-32) mul0 resp. mul1 unchanged for 65536/65536 keys. (4) Silenced trails (every active multiply has one differing operand and a zero co-operand, so the multipliers never differ): message Update activates >= k_msg(delta) >= 1 multiplies, round 1 >= 2 (distinct lanes), each later round >= 1, total >= R+2 (>= 2R+1 barring exact 64-bit additive cancellations); rigorous P[silenced] <= 2^(-32 k_msg) <= 2^-32 for one-packet messages, heuristic 2^-96, 2^-128, 2^-160, 2^-192 for R=1..4 under independent-uniform co-operands. Measured minima: unconditioned 1,3,7,15,23 cumulative active multiplies after msg,+1..+4 rounds (270 differences x 2^16 keys; the round-1 bound 3 is tight for 76 bit positions); trails with the message Update silenced by construction (2^16 keys x 20 cells): round-1 min 3, cumulative 4,8,16,24; 0 silenced multiplies / 0 product coincidences / 0 zero operands in 1.4e9 draws (0.33 expected). The bound covers only that class: the R=1 collisions (lane 3 bit 0: 1044491/2^20) all have mul0[3] changed and the four lane-0 words equal (lane locality), the 2 R=2 collisions in 2^20 are cancellations inside tau. (5) A universality proof stops at bounding |f^-1(0)| for f(key)=HH_R(k,M)-HH_R(k,M') over Z/2^64: f is not polynomial (XOR, lo/hi, byte permutation), root counting fails even for polynomials (2^63 X has 2^63 roots; (2^32 X)(2^32 Y)=0), and the rescuing assumption 'products are independent uniform words' is false: a'H-aH=(a'-a)H exactly (2^20/2^20), so the mul-difference is confined below bit 33 for 75.0% of keys (delta=+1, lane 3), P[bit63 of a product]=1/2-ln2/2=0.1534 (measured 0.1532), and for R>=1 both operands of the round-1 multiplies differ so even the exact-difference identity is lost. No effect on R>=3 was found or claimed; all results are structural facts about R<=2 plus proofs.

lemmas.statement: Lemma 1 (permutation). For every packet p, Update_p is a bijection of (Z/2^64)^16 with the explicit inverse F^-1 (v1 -= Zip(v0 pair)), E^-1 (v0 -= Zip(v1 pair)), then per lane D^-1 (mul1 ^= lo32(v0)*hi32(v1)), C^-1 (v0 -= mul1), B^-1 (mul0 ^= lo32(v1)*hi32(v0)), A^-1 (v1 -= mul0 + p). The finalization round rho(S)=Update_{Permute(v0)}(S) and the remainder step are bijections too (rho^-1 recovers Permute(v0) after C^-1). For equal-length M != M' and every key the final states differ, so every collision is a collision of the truncation tau = v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0] on two distinct states; every fibre of tau has exactly 2^960 states.
lemmas.proof_sketch: Each of steps A-F adds to, or XORs into, one coordinate a value computed from coordinates it does not modify (a transvection), hence is invertible by subtracting/XORing the same value; in the round the packet Permute(v0) is read from v0, which step A leaves unchanged. Equal-length messages M != M' have different padded packet sequences (every message byte occupies a packet position injectively for fixed s = |M| mod 32); at the first differing packet step A yields different v1 from equal states and all later steps are bijections. tau is a surjective group homomorphism, so its fibres are cosets of size 2^(1024-64).
lemmas.checked_numerically: mode `inverse 16`: 2^16 random (state, packet): UpdateInv(Update(S))=S 65536/65536; RoundInv(Round(S))=S 65536/65536; Update_p(S) != Update_p'(S) for random p != p' 65536/65536. Self-check on every run: our pipeline at R=4 == kExpected64 (65 lengths) and the 33-byte key2 vector; UpdateT == reference Update on 2^16 random states.

lemmas.statement: Lemma 2 (lane locality; R=0). (i) Lanes {0,1} of the state after Update_p depend only on lanes {0,1} before it and on p0, p1 (same for {2,3}); Reset and the remainder step act lane-wise; the tail packet puts tail bytes j < min(16, s&~3) into lanes 0,1 and every other tail byte into lanes 2,3. Hence HH_0(k,M) is a function of k0, k1, |M| and the message bytes at positions 32q+j, 0<=j<16, only. (ii) At R=0 any two same-length messages agreeing on those bytes collide for every key: any difference confined to lanes 2,3 of any packets, all 256 one-byte messages, the last s mod 4 bytes of a message with 1<=s<=15. (iv) Deterministic carry-free statement: the lane-0 words receive lane-1 values only through bytes 4,6,7 of v1[1] (at E) and bytes 4,6,7 of v0[1] (at F); a difference confined to bytes 2,3,5 of packet lane 1 (bits 16..31, 40..47) and lanes 2,3 leaves lane 0 untouched, hence collides at R=0, unless the addition at A carries into byte 4 or 6 of v1[1] or the addition at E carries into byte 4, 6 or 7 of v0[1].
lemmas.proof_sketch: Steps A-D act within a lane, E-F within a pair {0,1} or {2,3}; the only cross-pair operation is Permute, never applied at R=0; tau reads lane 0. The Zipper byte table (derived from the source: lane a receives own bytes {0,1,2,3,5} at positions [3->0,2->2,5->3,1->5,0->7] and partner bytes 4,6,7 at positions 1,4,6; lane b symmetric with own 1->4, 0->6 and partner 6->5, 7->7) shows lane 1's own bytes 2,3,5 land in bytes 2,0,3 of v0[1] and never in bytes 4,6,7 unless a carry crosses. The tail layout is read off HighwayHashUpdateRemainder (bytes 0..(s&~3)-1 in place; last s&3 bytes to packet bytes 16,17,18 when s<16; last four message bytes to 28..31 when s>=16).
lemmas.checked_numerically: mode `r0 20` and `active 16`: random lanes-2,3 differences collide 1048576/1048576 (32 B; 64 B first packet; 64 B both packets); all 256 one-byte messages equal for 65536/65536 keys; 256 values of byte 32 of a 33-byte message equal 65536/65536; bytes 44..46 of a 47-byte message 65536/65536 (byte 43 = lane-1 bit 24: 65285, a case of (iv)); every single bit of lanes 2,3: 65536/65536; lane 0 bits and lane-1 bits outside bytes 2,3,5: 0/65536 collisions; lane-1 bit 16: 65533, bit 17: 65535 (second stream 65526) of 65536.

lemmas.statement: Lemma 2, converse: 'a last-packet difference collides with probability exactly 1 at R=0 only if it is confined to lanes 2,3 (and the ignored tail bytes)'. Also the carry-model rates for lane-1 bytes 2,3,5: for a single flipped bit b the R=0 collision rate is (1-2^-(32-b))^2 for 16<=b<=23, 1-2^-(32-b) for 24<=b<=31, (1-2^-(48-b))^2 for 40<=b<=47.
lemmas.proof_sketch: No proof of the converse is offered: it is an existence statement (a key with distinct outputs) for each of 2^128-1 lane-0/1 differences, and the output involves carries of key-dependent sums. The carry-model rates follow from (iv) if the bits above the flipped bit in the sums at A and E are uniform and the two carry chains are independent, which is not proven (both depend on key[1]).
lemmas.assumption: Uniform, independent carry chains at steps A and E (heuristic; both are functions of key[1]).
lemmas.checked_numerically: 2^16 keys per bit (active_16.csv, R0 column), observed vs carry model: b=16: 65533 vs 65534; b=23: 65263 vs 65280; b=24: 65278 vs 65280; b=28: 61395 vs 61440; b=31: 33053 vs 32768; b=40: 65004 vs 65025; b=44: 57729 vs 57600; b=47: 16441 vs 16384. No lane-0/1 single bit collided for all 65536 keys (max 65535/65536).

lemmas.statement: Lemma 3 (one-step separation). For an additive difference delta != 0 in lane i of the packet from equal states: (a) lo32(v1[i]) differs iff lo32(delta) != 0; the high halves differ iff hi32(delta)+carry != 0 mod 2^32 (always if hi32(delta) not in {0, 2^32-1}; iff carry when hi32(delta)=0; iff no carry when hi32(delta)=2^32-1). (b) Since 32x32->64 products are exact integers, a'H - aH = (a'-a)H vanishes iff H=0: mul0[i] changes iff lo32(delta) != 0 and H = hi32(v0[i]) != 0; mul1[i] changes iff the high half of v1[i] changes and L = lo32(v0[i]+mul1[i]) != 0. (c) For one-packet messages (|M|<=32, full or remainder path) and a uniform key, H and L are independent uniform 32-bit words: P[H=0]=P[L=0]=2^-32, P[H=L=0]=2^-64; for |M|=32, P[carry]=lo32(delta)/2^32 exactly and the carry is independent of L. Exact corollary: mul0[i] is unchanged for every key with hi32(key[i]) = hi32(init0[i]); mul1[i] for every key with lo32(key[i]) = lo32(init0[i]) ^ (-lo32(init1[i]) mod 2^32).
lemmas.proof_sketch: (a) addition with carry. (b) m ^ aH = m ^ a'H iff the integers aH, a'H are equal iff (a'-a)H = 0 in Z (integral domain), and a != a'. (c) v0[i] = init0[i] ^ key[i] (+ (s<<32)+s on the remainder path) is a bijective image of the uniform key word, so its two halves are independent uniform; lo32(v1[i]) after A is (lo32(init1[i]) ^ hi32(key[i])) + const mod 2^32, uniform, and a function of hi32(key[i]) while L is a function of lo32(key[i]).
lemmas.checked_numerically: mode `onestep 20`: 60 cells (lanes 0-3 of 32-byte messages, lane 0 of 8-byte one-packet tail messages, lane 0 of the 40-byte two-Update tail, ten deltas each) x 2^20 keys: mul0 changed exactly when lo32 differed and mul1 exactly when hi32 differed (0 mismatches in 60 x 2^20); no zero co-operand in 60 x 2^20 draws (expected 0.03); high-half rates: delta=2^31: 0.4992-0.5005 (pred 0.5), delta=-2^31: 0.4994-0.5005 (0.5), delta=-2^30: 0.2492-0.2503 (0.25), delta=1: 0, delta=2^32 and 2^32-1: 1. Mode `cond 16`: in the subspace hi32(key[i])=hi32(init0[i]) mul0[i] unchanged 65536/65536 for delta=1 and delta=2^31 (mul1 changed for 32639-32937 keys = carry); in the subspace lo32(key[i])=lo32(init0[i])^(-lo32(init1[i])) mul1[i] unchanged 65536/65536 for delta=2^32 and 2^32+1 (mul0 changed for all keys).

lemmas.statement: Lemma 4 (silenced trails), rigorous part. A multiply is active if an operand differs; a trail is silenced if every active multiply has exactly one differing operand and its co-operand is 0 (then all 8(R+1) products coincide, mul0/mul1 never differ, the difference lives in (v0,v1)). (a) The message Update activates >= k_msg(delta) = #{i: lo32(delta_i)!=0} + #{i: hi32(delta_i) not in {0,2^32-1}} >= #{i: delta_i != 0} >= 1 multiplies for every key, each with one differing operand; for one-packet messages P[message Update silenced] <= 2^(-32 k_msg(delta)) <= 2^-32. (b) On a silenced trail round 1 activates >= 2 multiplies in two different lanes. (c) Every later round activates >= 1. (d) A silenced trail through Update + R rounds activates >= R+2 multiplies (R>=1), each needing a zero co-operand. The bound covers only the silenced class: not product coincidences a'H'=aH with both operands differing, and not trails where the multipliers differ but the difference never reaches lane 0 or cancels inside tau (the observed R=1 collisions are of that kind).
lemmas.proof_sketch: (a) Lemma 3(a): lo32(delta_i)!=0 activates M0_i, else hi32(delta_i)!=0 with no carry activates M1_i; v0 is untouched before B and D so co-operands are equal; co-operands of different lanes depend on different key words and H_i, L_i on disjoint halves. (b) After the message Update v0 differs in some lane a of every pair meeting J: v0 after E = (v0+mul1) + Zip(v1_A) with v0+mul1 equal and Zip a bijection of the pair. In round 1, hi32(v0[a]) differing activates M0_a, else lo32(v0[a]) differing makes lo32(v0[a]+mul1[a]) differ and activates M1_a; if J is inside one pair, the other pair's lane a^2 receives sigma(v0[a]) at step A with nothing else differing, so v1[a^2] differs and activates M0 or M1 there; if J meets both pairs each pair has such a lane. (c) Step A is a bijection, so after it some v0[i] (untouched by A) or v1[i] differs, activating a multiply of lane i. (d) sum.
lemmas.checked_numerically: mode `cond 16` (message Update silenced by construction in the density-2^-32 subspaces, 20 cells x 2^16 keys): all 8 multipliers equal and difference confined to (v0,v1) of the pair for 65536/65536 keys in every fully silenced cell; minimum active multiplies in round 1: 3 (6 with both co-operands zeroed); rounds 2-4 minima 4-8; minimum cumulative after 1..4 rounds 4, 8, 16, 24 (bound 3,4,5,6). Mode `active 16` (256 single bits + 14 word-level, 2^16 keys each): minimum cumulative active 1, 3, 7, 15, 23 after msg, +1..+4 rounds; 0 silenced multiplies, 0 product coincidences, 0 zero operands in 1,415,577,600 operand draws (0.33 expected). Mode `r1coll 20`: 1044491/2^20 R=1 collisions for lane 3 bit 0, all with mul0[3] changed and all four lane-0 words equal; 2 R=2 collisions, both with distinct lane-0 states.

lemmas.statement: Lemma 4, heuristic part: P[silenced trail through Update + R rounds] <= 2^(-32(R+2)) = 2^-96, 2^-128, 2^-160, 2^-192 for R = 1..4; and, barring exact 64-bit additive cancellations Delta x = -Delta y between two nonzero differences meeting at step A or E, every round activates >= 2 multiplies, giving >= 2R+1 active multiplies (2^-32(2R+1) under the same model).
lemmas.proof_sketch: Count from the rigorous lemma; each active multiply on a silenced trail needs its co-operand (a 32-bit state half) to be zero. Only the message-Update co-operands are provably uniform and independent (Lemma 3(c)); the round co-operands are functions of the whole key and are modelled as independent uniform 32-bit words. The >= 2 per round statement fails only if an additive cancellation makes a pair carry no difference after step A, or v0 of a pair returns to equality at E.
lemmas.assumption: The R+1 co-operands met in the finalization rounds are (conditionally) independent uniform 32-bit words; for multi-packet messages also that the pre-last-packet state halves are uniform. Not provable from the structure.
lemmas.checked_numerically: Consistent with, but not verifiable at, our sample sizes: 0 zero operands in 1.4e9 unconditioned operand draws (0.33 expected at 2^-32 each); observed active counts far exceed the bounds (min 3 in round 1 both unconditioned and with the message Update silenced; cumulative minima 7/8, 15/16, 23/24 after 2, 3, 4 rounds).

lemmas.statement: Lemma 5 (where a universality proof stops). With f(k) = HH_R(k,M) - HH_R(k,M') in Z/2^64, a polynomial-hashing-style proof needs (P1) f not identically 0 and (P2) a bound on |f^-1(0)| from the algebraic form of f. (P1) fails at R=0 for lanes-2,3 differences. (P2) fails for every R at the first active multiply: (i) f is not a polynomial over Z/2^64 (XOR with key-dependent words, lo/hi splits, byte permutations), and over GF(2) its bits have degree up to 64 so P[g=0] <= 1-2^-deg g is vacuous; (ii) root counting fails in Z/2^64 even for polynomials: 2^63 X has degree 1 and 2^63 roots, X^2 has 2^32 roots, (2^32 X)(2^32 Y) vanishes identically; (iii) the assumption that would close the gap, 'the products a_t H_t (or the words (m ^ a'H') - (m ^ aH) they contribute) are independent uniform words', gives P[f=0]=2^-64 at once but is false: a'H - aH = (a'-a)H exactly (magnitude < 2^32 |a'-a|), a product of uniform halves has P[bit 63 = 1] = 1/2 - ln(2)/2 = 0.1534 and P[bit 0 = 1] = 1/4, and successive operands are functions of the same key bits; for R >= 1 the round-1 multiplies of the differing lane have both operands differing so even the exact-difference identity is lost (a'H' - aH = (a'-a)H' + a(H'-H)).
lemmas.proof_sketch: The 2^63 X example: 2^63 X = 0 mod 2^64 iff X is even. P[bit 63 of aH = 1] = P[XY >= 1/2] for uniform X,Y on [0,1] = 1 - 1/2 + (1/2) ln(1/2). P[aH odd] = 1/4. The exact difference is Lemma 3(b). Both operands differing in round 1 is Lemma 4(b): v0[a] differs from the Zipper and v1[a] from step A in the same lane.
lemmas.checked_numerically: mode `products 20`: P[bit63(a*h)=1] = 0.15323 on 2^20 uniform pairs (exact 0.15343); P[bit0=1] = 0.24958 (1/4); a'h - ah == (a'-a)h as integers 1048576/1048576; mul0[3] XOR-difference after the message Update for delta=+1 in lane 3 (2^20 keys): bytes 0-7 differ with frequencies 0.9961, 0.9961, 0.9961, 0.9962, 0.5005, 0.0020, 0, 0; confined below bit 33 for 75.00% of keys, below bit 40 for 99.80%.

proofs.where_proof_stops: Step (P2): bounding the number of keys with f(k) = HH_R(k,M) - HH_R(k,M') = 0. Concretely, already at R = 0 with a difference in lane 0 of a 32-byte message the collision event is Delta v0[0] + Delta v1[0] + [(init0[0] ^ aH) - (init0[0] ^ a'H)] + [(init1[0] ^ L h) - (init1[0] ^ L h')] = 0 (mod 2^64), where a, a', h, h' are halves of v1[0] = (init1[0] ^ rot32(key[0])) + init0[0] + p[0] and H = hi32(init0[0] ^ key[0]), L = lo32((init0[0] ^ key[0]) + init1[0]): a function of the single key word key[0] mixing XOR (GF(2)-linear), additions mod 2^32/2^64 (carries) and integer products of 32-bit halves. No tool bounds its zero set: it is not a polynomial over Z/2^64, and Z/2^64 has no root bound anyway (2^63 X vanishes on half the ring; (2^32 X)(2^32 Y) on all of it), while over GF(2) the product bits have algebraic degree up to 32 and the Boolean degree bound is vacuous. The one exact tool that survives, Lemma 3(b) (a'H - aH = (a'-a)H, nonzero unless H = 0), only separates the multiplier words after the message Update; it does not bound how often the XOR-difference (m ^ aH) - (m ^ a'H) cancels the other three summands. The assumption that would finish the proof, that the products (or their contributed words Delta_t) are independent uniform 64-bit words, is false: the two products share the operand H and differ by exactly (a'-a)H, so Delta_t is confined to the low 33+log2|a'-a| bits (75% of keys below bit 33 for delta = +1, bytes 5-7 differ with frequency <= 0.002), single products are biased (bit 63 set w.p. 0.1534), and the operands are functions of the same key halves. For R >= 1 the first round-1 multiply of the differing lane has BOTH operands differing (v0[a] via the Zipper, v1[a] via step A), so even the exact-difference identity is lost and P[a'H' = aH] has no structure to bound; this is the first step for R >= 1 that cannot be taken.
proofs.caveats: (1) The exact key-probabilities in Lemma 3(c) and the rigorous 2^(-32 k_msg) bound in Lemma 4 hold for one-packet messages (|M| <= 32, full or remainder path); for multi-packet messages the pre-last-packet state is not provably uniform and those numbers are heuristic (the 40-byte onestep cells matched the same rates but are outside the lemma). (2) The 2^-32(R+2) silenced-trail bound is heuristic beyond the message Update (independent-uniform co-operands assumed); only >= R+2 active multiplies and the 2^-32 factor from the first one are rigorous; the '>= 2 per round' count assumes no exact 64-bit additive cancellation. (3) The silenced-trail class is narrow and is NOT the mechanism of the observed R=1,2 collisions (lane locality and cancellation inside tau); Lemma 4 bounds nothing about the true collision probability at R<=2. (4) The converse of Lemma 2 (only lanes 2,3 collide with probability exactly 1 at R=0) is unproven; lane-1 bytes 2,3,5 come within a carry of it (up to 65535/65536), the carry-model rates for them are checked, not proven. (5) 2^16-2^20 keys cannot observe 2^-32 events (zero co-operands: 0 seen, 0.33 expected), so the exception clauses of Lemma 3 were verified only on conditional subspaces of density 2^-32 (2^16 keys each), stated as such. (6) Lemma 5 is a statement about why the standard proof technique cannot proceed, not an impossibility theorem: a bound obtained by other means is not excluded. (7) No collision or bias at R >= 3 was found or claimed; the R=1/R=2 counts reproduce the earlier panel (lane 3 bit 0: 0.996 at R=1, ~2^-19 at R=2) with independent code and keys. (8) The r0-mode '47-byte control' byte 43 is itself lane-1 bit 24 (a Lemma 2(iv) case), so it is not a control; it is labelled accordingly in the files. (9) Single-threaded runs, no timing claims; all modes rerun the published-vector self-check and abort on failure.

proofs.summary: PROOF-SIDE RESULT for HighwayHash-64, one 32-byte packet, R=1 (published hash is R=4). (1) Closed form of the R=1 lane-0 output (Lemma 1, verified against the reference on 200,000 random key/message pairs): lanes 2,3 enter only through Z2=v0[2] (which feeds U0, the ONLY word entering the two lane-0 multiplies) and Z3=v0[3] (which feeds only byte shuffles/additions). Differences routed into Z3 (A3 bytes {0,1,2,3,5}, A2 bytes {4,6,7}) form a ZERO-MULTIPLY sector where everything is provable; z3 (4.15.4) certifies bit-vector statements on a relaxed model (A2,A3,B3,T,U0,W0,W1 free 64-bit words; sound for 'for every key'), and a 'slice lemma' (a key byte acting bijectively on a byte quantity up to r carry offsets gives Pr<=(r+1)/256, exact when r=0) turns byte events into probabilities. (2) THEOREM 1, certain collisions at R=1, for every m: Pr[H1(m+e3)=H1(m)]>=1-9*2^-8 (measured 0.99602 at 2^22 keys), Pr[H1(m+2^32 e2)=H1(m)]>=1-7*2^-8 (0.98834), Pr[H1(m+2^56 e2)=H1(m)]>=1-3*2^-8 (0.99225): z3-proved sufficient byte conditions + slice bounds. (3) THEOREM 2, upper bounds at R=1, for every m: m+2^8 e3: <=2^-22; m+2^16 e3: <=2^-8; m+2^24 e3: <=3*2^-8; m+2^40 e3: <=2^-8+9*2^-16; m+2^48 e2: <=3*2^-8 (measured 0,0,0,0,1 collisions in 2^22 keys). z3 also REFUTED my hand claim that these classes never collide: two byte deltas in one 32-bit half combine into changes like 0xFFFF0001 that skip byte 4; m+2^48 e2 really collides with rate ~2^-23 (1/2^22 observed, witness mechanism exhibited). (4) PROPOSITION 3, the obstruction: in the multiply-active branch (A3.b5=ff for m+2^40 e3, prob 2^-8) the collision condition is exactly (M^(P+h))-(M^P)=0xFEFF0000FFFFFFFF with M=mul0[0] mask, P=lo32(U0)*hi32(X0), h=hi32(X0); concrete keys show the XOR mask destroys the additive difference h; z3 proves the equation forces h odd and 25 specific bits of M and 24 bits of P; M depends only on hi32(k0) and m0, and an exhaustive 2^32 count gives 196 admissible values (2^-24.4) for m0=09f1fd9d03f0a9b4, so that generic sub-case contributes <=2^-32.4 for that message; conditional sampling inside the branch: 0 collisions in 2^22 keys. The proof stops at bounding the remaining sub-cases uniformly in m and at the min-entropy of hi32(Z2) over (k2,k3); at R>=2 every trail is multiply-active (R=2 rate for m+e3: 3/2^22 here, 2/2^20 in the earlier sweep). Dichotomy: provable = zero-multiply sector at R=1 (best certified upper bound 2^-22, lower bound 0.988); breakable at R=4 needs a trail passing four rounds of key-masked multiplies at 2^-8..2^-32 per event; sampling decides only rates >=2^-30.

lemmas.statement: Lemma 1 (closed form, R=1, one packet). With A_i=(C1_i^swap32(k_i))+C0_i+m_i, B_i=(C0_i^k_i)+C1_i, M0_i=C0_i^(lo32 A_i * hi32(C0_i^k_i)), M1_i=C1_i^(lo32 B_i * hi32 A_i), X0=B0+f0(A0,A1), X1=B1+f1(A0,A1), Z2=B2+f0(A2,A3), Z3=B3+f1(A2,A3), Y0=A0+f0(X0,X1), Y1=A1+f1(X0,X1), U0=Y0+M0_0+swap32(Z2), W0=X0+M1_0, T=Y1+M0_1, U1=T+swap32(Z3), W1=X1+M1_1, a=W0+f0(U0,U1), b=W1+f1(U0,U1), v=U0+f0(a,b): H_1(m) = a+v+[M0_0^(lo32 U0*hi32 X0)]+[M1_0^(lo32 W0*hi32 U0)]. Here f0(x,y)=[x.b3,y.b4,x.b2,x.b5,y.b6,x.b1,y.b7,x.b0], f1(x,y)=[y.b3,x.b4,y.b2,y.b5,y.b1,x.b6,y.b0,x.b7]. Consequently the R=1 output ignores v1[2],v1[3],mul0[2..3],mul1[2..3]; lanes 2,3 enter only through Z2 (-> U0 -> both lane-0 multiplies) and Z3 (-> U1 -> byte shuffles and additions only).
lemmas.proof_sketch: Unfold Reset, the message Update (lane loop, then ZipperMergeAndAdd on (v1[0],v1[1]) into v0 and on the new v0 into v1, same for lanes 2,3), Permute(v0) = swap32 of lanes (2,3,0,1), and one more Update restricted to lane 0 and the words it reads. The byte tables f0/f1 are read off the reference mask expressions.
lemmas.checked_numerically: alg.c `check 200000 7`: 0 mismatches between the closed form (and all ten post-absorption words X0,X1,Y0,Y1,Z2,Z3,M0_0,M0_1,M1_0,M1_1) and HighwayHash64R(.,32,key,1) on 200,000 random (key,message) pairs; byte tables agree with the literal ZipperMergeAndAdd on 300,000 random inputs; the copied C reproduces all 65 published kExpected64 vectors and the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4.

lemmas.statement: Lemma 2 (zero-multiply sector). A difference confined to A3 bytes {0,1,2,3,5} or A2 bytes {4,6,7} changes Z3 but not Z2; then U0, X0, W0 and both multiply terms are unchanged and H_1'-H_1=(a'-a)+(v'-v) is a function of (A2,A3,B3,T,U0,W0,W1) only. Relaxed model: treating these seven words as free 64-bit variables, any z3-UNSAT statement about H_1'=H_1 holds for every key and message.
lemmas.proof_sketch: f0(A2,A3) reads A2 bytes {0,1,2,3,5} and A3 bytes {4,6,7}; f1 reads the complementary bytes; Z2 only feeds U0; lane-1 mul words never reach the lane-0 output. Freeing key-derived words enlarges the reachable set, so UNSAT (no collision / always collision) transfers to the real hash.
lemmas.checked_numerically: Consistent with the `rates` split (#excluded column): the multiply-active event A3.b5=ff occurred 16406 times in 2^22 keys (expected 16384) etc.

lemmas.statement: Slice lemma. If for every fixing of the other key bits a byte quantity Q = phi(kappa)+e(kappa) mod 256 with phi a bijection of one key byte kappa (a byte of some k_i, or of A2/A3, which are bijective images of k2/k3) and e(kappa) in {0..r}, then Pr[Q=v] <= (r+1)/256, with equality 1/256 when r=0. Applications used: bytes of A_i uniform; Z3.b7, U1.b3, b.b0 bijective in A2.b7; Z3.b3 bijective in k3.b3; U1.b1 bijective in A2.b6; Z3.b5 bijective in A2.b6; U1.b0 via k3.b5 (r<=2), U1.b2 via k3.b4 (r<=3), U1.b4 via k3.b7 (r=1), U1.b5 and b.b3 via A2.b4 (r=1,2), Z3.b6 via k3.b4 (r<=2).
lemmas.proof_sketch: For each offset value e there is at most one kappa with phi(kappa)=v-e; kappa is uniform and independent of the other key bits. Each application checks that the chosen key byte enters the target byte exactly once bijectively (through an XOR with a constant followed by additions with no carry-in from kappa-dependent bytes) and elsewhere only through carries.
lemmas.checked_numerically: Not separately sampled; the exclusion-event counts in rates_22_msg24301.md match the exact 2^-8/2^-16 predictions (16301, 16406, 16305 of 2^22 for 2^-8 events; 52 for a 2^-16 event).

lemmas.proof_sketch: z3 proves (relax2_out.txt) that the conditions (i) A3.b0!=ff, not(Z3.b6=Z3.b7=ff), U1.b2!=ff, not(b.b2=b.b3=ff); (ii) A2.b4!=ff, not(Z3.b1=b2=b3=ff), U1.b5!=ff, b.b3!=ff; (iii) Z3.b7!=ff, U1.b3!=ff, b.b0!=ff force H_1'=H_1 in the relaxed model (mechanism: the changed byte is routed by f1 into a byte of U1 and then into a byte of b that f0(a,b) never reads). Union bound over the complementary byte events with the slice lemma: (i) 2^-8+2^-8+4*2^-8+3*2^-8, (ii) 2^-8+2^-8+2*2^-8+3*2^-8, (iii) 3*2^-8 (all exact via A2.b7).

lemmas.proof_sketch: Split on whether Z2 changes (carry of A3+delta reaching A3.b4, resp. A2+delta reaching A2.b5): exactly 2^-24, 2^-16, 2^-8, 2^-8, 0. In the Z2-unchanged branch z3 proves a collision forces, respectively: hi32(Z3)=ffffffff; A3.b2=ff; U1.b4=U1.b5=ff; Z3.b3=ff and U1.b0=ff; A2.b6=ff or Z3.b7=ff or U1.b1=ff (relax2_out.txt, relax3_out.txt). Slice counting: Pr[hi32 Z3=ffffffff]<=3*2^-24 (for each k3.b4 one A2.b6 gives Z3.b5=ff, then one A2.b7 gives Z3.b7=ff, and Z3.b6 is a bijection of k3.b4 up to <=2 offsets); Pr[U1.b4=ff]<=2^-7; Pr[Z3.b3=ff and U1.b0=ff]<=9*2^-16 (slices k3.b3, k3.b5); Pr[U1.b1=ff]=2^-8 exactly.

lemmas.statement: Proposition 3 (reduced equation of the multiply-active branch). For m'=m+2^40 e_3 and a key with A3.b5=ff, generically U0'=U0+1, U1'=U1+2^56-1, the zipper part changes by exactly 2^56+2^48-2^32+1, and with L=lo32(U0), h=hi32(X0), P=L*h, M=M0_0: H_1'=H_1 iff (M^(P+h))-(M^P) = 0xFEFF0000FFFFFFFF (mod 2^64). Every solution has h odd, M_0=not h_1, M[32..46]=0, M[47..54]=1, M[55]=0, M[56]=1, P[32..55]=1. M depends only on hi32(k0) and m0; for m0=09f1fd9d03f0a9b4 exactly 196 of the 2^32 values of hi32(k0) satisfy the forced pattern, so for that message this sub-case contributes at most 2^-8*196/2^32 ~ 2^-32.4.
lemmas.proof_sketch: Product difference (L+1)h-Lh=h is exact (tool b), but the state stores M^P; with x=M^P and carry vectors gamma of x+c, kappa of P+h, the identity x^(x+c)=P^(P+h) gives gamma_i^kappa_i=c_i^h_i for all i; c=FEFF0000FFFFFFFF has bits 0..31=1, 32..47=0, 48..55=1, 56=0, 57..63=1 and h has bits 32..63=0, which pins the two monotone carry chains from bit 32 up. z3 proves the pattern (UNSAT of equation AND NOT pattern, P free). The count is an exhaustive 2^32 enumeration (alg.c `mpattern`).

lemmas.statement: Conjecture (heuristic bound for the multiply-active branch). For m'=m+2^40 e_3 the multiply-active branch contributes at most about 2^-8 * 2^-24 * 2^-24 (M pattern times P pattern), i.e. Pr[H_1(m')=H_1(m)] is about 9*2^-16 in total (dominated by the zero-multiply mechanisms), and more generally every R=1 pair confined to lane 2/3 bytes has rate <= ~2^-15.
lemmas.proof_sketch: Would follow from the reduced equation if L=lo32(U0) were uniform and independent of (M,h) given (k0,k1) (a 'random product' assumption) and the non-generic sub-cases were handled the same way.
lemmas.assumption: min-entropy of hi32(Z2)=hi32(B2+f0(A2,A3)) over (k2,k3) is ~32 bits given everything else (only 15 bits are proved, from A3 bytes 6,7), and the finitely many non-generic sub-cases (carries in U0, U1, Z3, hi32(Z2) wrap) behave like the generic one.
lemmas.checked_numerically: 0 collisions in 2^22 conditional keys inside the branch (sensitivity ~2^-22 conditional, ~2^-30 overall); output-difference probes inside the branch look uniform (low byte zero 16272 vs 16384 ideal).

proofs.where_proof_stops: The first step a proof cannot take is bounding Pr_key[(M ^ (P + h)) - (M ^ P) = c] once a difference reaches a lane-0 multiply: here M = mul0[0] = C0_0 ^ (lo32(A_0)*hi32(C0_0^k0)) is a key-dependent XOR mask, P = lo32(U0)*hi32(X0) and h = hi32(X0) are other functions of the same key, and the additive difference h of the product is scrambled by the mask (obstruct output: h=5d75b8ab becomes 000000015e894889). The equation is not polynomial over any ring (XOR, modular add and 32x32->64 multiply mix), so no root counting applies; the carry-chain analysis (z3-proved) reduces it to forced bit patterns on M (25 bits), P (24 bits) and h (2 bits), and the M part can be counted exactly only by 2^32 enumeration for ONE fixed m0 (196/2^32 here), not uniformly in m; the P part needs the min-entropy of lo32(U0) = lo32(Y0+M0_0) + hi32(Z2), i.e. of hi32(Z2) = hi32(B2 + f0(A2,A3)) as a function of (k2,k3), where hi32(k2) enters both B2 and A2 and nothing proves it acts injectively (only 15 bits from A3 bytes 6,7 are certifiable, giving a useless 2^-15 point bound); and the finitely many non-generic carry sub-cases each change the constant c and were not enumerated. Concretely for m+2^40 e_3 at R=1 the certified bound is 2^-8 + 9*2^-16 while the truth is presumably ~2^-15 or below. At R=2 every trail crosses Permute into lanes whose multiplies are active with key-dependent masks (the earlier lens' 2^-19 rate for m+e_3 at R=2 lives entirely there), so nothing at R>=2 is provable in either direction with these tools.
proofs.caveats: (1) All theorems are for messages of exactly 32 bytes (one packet, no UpdateRemainder) and R=1; the published hash is R=4 and nothing here bounds it. (2) The z3 certificates are on a relaxed model (seven key-derived words freed); this is sound for 'for every key' conclusions (UNSAT results) but SAT witnesses need not be key-realizable; the probability bounds then come from hand-verified slice arguments and union bounds, which are crude (e.g. the certified 0.965 vs measured 0.996; certified 2^-8 vs measured 0/2^22 for m+2^16 e_3). (3) The slice-lemma applications (which key byte is bijective, how many carry offsets) were derived by hand from the closed form and not machine-checked; a mistake there would loosen a constant factor, not the mechanism. (4) Numerics: one base message (splitmix seed 24301) and 2^22 keys per class (3 x 1,398,101), seed 1; conditional sampling 2^22 keys inside A3.b5=ff, seed 9; theorems are stated for all m but only this m was sampled; the mpattern count 196 is exact but for this m0 only. (5) My initial hand analysis claimed these zero-multiply classes never collide; z3 refuted that (multi-byte deltas combining into e.g. 0xFFFF0001), and m+2^48 e_2 really collides at ~2^-23; treat the z3-certified necessary conditions, not the hand narrative, as the proof. (6) The shared context said R=1 has no full collisions for plain complements; that is true for complements but single-byte additive differences into Z3 collide with probability ~0.99 (already found by the structured-differences lens; here proved). (7) Machine was heavily loaded (load 150-270); no timing claims; <=3 threads used (2 threads while z3 ran). (8) z3 4.15.4, Python 3.14.7, Apple clang 17; the copied C reproduces all published vectors at R=4 (vectors_check: OK, hh_test_upstream: Test success).

proofVerdicts.lemma: Lemma 1 (permutation). For every packet p, Update_p is a bijection of (Z/2^64)^16 with the explicit inverse F^-1 (v1 -= Zip(v0 pair)), E^-1 (v0 -= Zip(v1 pair)), then per lane D^-1 (mul1 ^= lo32(v0)*hi32(v1)), C^-1 (v0 -= mul1), B^-1 (mul0 ^= lo32(v1)*hi32(v0)), A^-1 (v1 -= mul0 + p). The finalization round rho(S)=Update_{Permute(v0)}(S) and the remainder step are bijections too (rho^-1 recovers Permute(v0) after C^-1). For equal-length M != M' and every key the final states differ, so every collision is a collision of the truncation tau = v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0] on two distinct states; every fibre of tau has exactly 2^960 states.

verdict.reasoning: Checked every step of Lemma 1 against the unmodified reference C (sha256 fb316726...): the Zip byte maps Zip_a=[x3,y4,x2,x5,y6,x1,y7,x0], Zip_b=[y3,x4,y2,y5,y1,x6,y0,x7], Permute, the remainder layout (bytes 0..(s&~3)-1 in place; s&16 -> last 4 tail bytes to 28..31; else tail bytes to 16,17,18), exact 32x32->64 products, and the inverse order F^-1,E^-1,D^-1,C^-1,B^-1,A^-1 (RoundInv recovers Permute(v0) after C^-1) are all correct; tau is a surjective homomorphism so fibres have 2^960 states. The FALSE clause is "for equal-length M != M' and every key the final states differ". The proof handles only the first differing packet ("the remaining steps, packets and rounds are bijections"): when a later packet differs too, Update_p and Update_p' are different bijections, and Update_p(X)=Update_p'(X') iff X,X' agree on v0,mul0,mul1 and differ in v1 by p'-p (B..F never read the packet). Explicit construction, valid for EVERY key (known key): difference in lane 0 of packets 1,2,3. Packet 1: v1_A[0] differs in bytes 2,3 by +-1 (no carry, D silent; B gives mul0 ^= aH vs a'H, H=hi32(v0_init[0]); E gives v0_1'[0]=v0_1[0]+D, D=(b3'-b3)+2^16(b2'-b2); P1 chosen so lo32(v0_1[0])=0x80000000 and hi32(v0_1[0])=H via the four high bytes of Zip_a). Packet 2: v1_A(2)[0]=(0|b0 b1 b2' b3'), v1_A'(2)[0]=(0|b0 b1 b2 b3): B XORs a'H/aH again so mul0 is equal, hi32=0 silences D, Zip_a'-Zip_a=-D cancels v0[0], Zip_b reads bytes 4,6,7 only so v0[1] is equal; state differs only in v1[0]. Packet 3 (or 8-byte tail after Rem_8): P3'[0]=P3[0]+(v1_2[0]+mul0_2[0])-(v1_2'[0]+mul0_2'[0]) -> identical 1024-bit state. Results (counter.c, out/counter_16.txt): kTestKey1, 96 B: M=fea24c741343cab5294be8e9b72a3ebdcb736aa1a493be87440da55789c0715a5584323df3ee5a47782cad68e1d645c39342623a2af37de4350210ca24b7ca08bf94a9229452a4df87283eef45794c1a9a2aadd00a8d14a3592700d4d9d0d162, M'=fea24d751343cab5294be8e9b72a3ebdcb736aa1a493be87440da55789c0715a5584dedda0a83847782cad68e1d645c39342623a2af37de4350210ca24b7ca08bf94aa239452a4df87283eef45794c1a9a2aadd00a8d14a3592700d4d9d0d162; reference HighwayHash64 = 80a08f489ebe8a20 for both, HH_R equal for R=0,1,2,3,4, HighwayHash128 and 256 equal. Same for kTestKey2 (HH64=7a722797696442eb) and a 72-byte tail variant (49f9d2b462db424c). Sweep: 2^16 uniformly random keys (seed 0x5EED0001): identical internal state 65536/65536 (96 B) and 65536/65536 (72 B); reference HighwayHash64 collides 65536/65536; all R=0..4 collide 65536/65536; M!=M' always. Control: each fixed pair collides for 0/65536 fresh random keys at every R, so this is a known-key internal collision, not a random-key attack. Also checked: one Update from equal states with packets differing in one lane leaves v0 different 65536/65536, so the earliest merge is two packets after the first difference. Self-check on every run: reference == kExpected64 (65 lengths) and the 33-byte key2 vector; my hashR(.,4) == the same vectors; hh_test_ref prints "Test success". Files: experiment/attack/refute-lemma-0/{counter.c,README.md,out/counter_16.txt,hh_ref/c/}. Commands: cc -O2 -std=gnu99 -Ihh_ref counter.c -o out/counter && nice -n 10 ./out/counter 16. (That directory also holds files from another agent: hh/, refute.c, lane-locality-fable/; not mine, untouched.)
verdict.corrected_claim: Lemma 1 (corrected). For every packet p, Update_p is a bijection of (Z/2^64)^16 with the stated explicit inverse; rho and Rem_s are bijections; tau is a surjective homomorphism with fibres of exactly 2^960 states. For equal-length M != M' whose padded packet sequences differ in exactly ONE packet position, or in exactly two ADJACENT positions, the final states differ for every key (a merge can only occur at step A of a later differing packet and requires the two states to differ only in v1, but immediately after the first differing packet v0 already differs). In general the clause is false: for EVERY key there exist explicit equal-length pairs (96 bytes with three differing full packets, or 72 bytes with two packets plus the 8-byte tail; differences confined to lane 0) with identical 1024-bit internal states, hence colliding for every number of finalization rounds R and for HighwayHash64/128/256 alike. These pairs depend on the key (known-key construction; a fixed pair collides for 0/2^16 other keys), so 'every collision is a truncation collision of two distinct states' holds only for random keys with overwhelming probability, not for every key.

proofVerdicts.lemma: Lemma 2 (lane locality; R=0). (i) Lanes {0,1} of the state after Update_p depend only on lanes {0,1} before it and on p0, p1 (same for {2,3}); Reset and the remainder step act lane-wise; the tail packet puts tail bytes j < min(16, s&~3) into lanes 0,1 and every other tail byte into lanes 2,3. Hence HH_0(k,M) is a function of k0, k1, |M| and the message bytes at positions 32q+j, 0<=j<16, only. (ii) At R=0 any two same-length messages agreeing on those bytes collide for every key: any difference confined to lanes 2,3 of any packets, all 256 one-byte messages, the last s mod 4 bytes of a message with 1<=s<=15. (iv) Deterministic carry-free statement: the lane-0 words receive lane-1 values only through bytes 4,6,7 of v1[1] (at E) and bytes 4,6,7 of v0[1] (at F); a difference confined to bytes 2,3,5 of packet lane 1 (bits 16..31, 40..47) and lanes 2,3 leaves lane 0 untouched, hence collides at R=0, unless the addition at A carries into byte 4 or 6 of v1[1] or the addition at E carries into byte 4, 6 or 7 of v0[1].

verdict.reasoning: Audited every step of Lemma 2 against the unmodified reference C (sha256 fb316726...; my copy of highwayhash_test prints "Test success"). ZipperMergeAndAdd(v1=lane b, v0=lane a) gives addend_a=[x3,y4,x2,x5,y6,x1,y7,x0], addend_b=[y3,x4,y2,y5,y1,x6,y0,x7] exactly as the lemma's Zip_a/Zip_b, so lane 0 receives lane-1 bytes 4,6,7 only (at E from v1[1], at F from v0[1]); steps A-D are lane-wise, E/F pair-wise, Permute is only reached through PermuteAndUpdate (never at R=0), the output reads lane 0; Reset and the remainder pre-steps are lane-wise and the tail layout (bytes 0..(s&~3)-1 in place, last s&3 bytes to packet 16..18 for s<16, last 4 bytes to 28..31 for s>=16) is as stated. Only wording nit: for s=16..19 tail bytes 12..15 are duplicated into lane 3 as well as lane 1 (harmless: they are j<16 bytes). For (iv), the three "unless" events read as carry differences (into bit 32 and bit 48 at A, into bit 32 at E) are exactly the events that make bytes 4,6,7 of v1[1] or of v0[1] differ; "byte 6 or 7 at E" is redundant. Independent numerics (my own pipeline built on the reference's public functions; R=4 reproduces all 66 vectors; my tail transcription validated vs ProcessAll for lengths 1..160 x 512 keys): (a) exact (iv) test, lengths 32,64,96,48,60,44,47,63, 2^17 keys each, random XOR difference in packet-lane-1 bytes 2,3,5 plus all of lanes 2,3: NC <=> lane-0 state equal and NC => 64-bit collision, 0 violations in 8x2^17 trials (len 32: 44222 NC, 44222 collide; 86850 not-NC, 0 collide). (b) Ignored-byte map: all 4656 (length 0..96, byte) cells at 2^10 keys agree with the lemma's formula except three lane-1-byte-2 cells that collided 1024/1024 by chance; at 2^16 keys those bytes fail for ~170 keys (65359/65536, 65367/65536), i.e. sensitive, as the lemma says. Bulk: random length 0..160 with ALL lemma-ignored bytes re-randomised: R=0 collisions 131072/131072 (R=1 control 0/127120); all 256 one-byte messages equal for 131072/131072 keys; k2,k3 re-randomised: R=0 output equal 131072/131072. (c) 128 single bits of lanes 0,1 at 2^16 keys: lane 0 and lane-1 bits outside bytes 2,3,5: 0 collisions; bits 16..31,40..47 match the carry model within ~1% (bit 16: 65533, bit 31: 32697, bit 47: 16236); largest deviation bit 20 (65473 vs model 65504, z~-5.5) because the model omits the in-byte carry from byte 2 into byte 3 at A, a refinement of the stated model, not a refutation. Proof complete, numerical claims reproduce, no counterexample found. Files: experiment/attack/refute-lemma-0/lane-locality-fable/{README.md,ll_check.c,key23_check.c,out/*.txt} (a sibling agent also writes into refute-lemma-0/; its files were left alone).
verdict.corrected_claim: Lemma 2 stands as stated. Sharpened reading of (iv): with the difference confined to bytes 2,3,5 of packet lane 1 (plus lanes 2,3), the lane-0 state after Update is equal IF AND ONLY IF the carry into bit 32 and the carry into bit 48 at (A) and the carry into bit 32 at (E) are the same in both executions (the "byte 6 or 7 at E" clause is redundant); checked with 0 violations on 8 x 2^17 keys. Wording nit in (i): for s in 16..19 tail bytes 12..15 are also duplicated into lane 3. The carry-model rates for bits 16..23 slightly overpredict (bit 20: 65473 vs 65504 of 65536) because of the in-byte carry from byte 2 into byte 3 at (A).

proofVerdicts.lemma: Lemma 2, converse: 'a last-packet difference collides with probability exactly 1 at R=0 only if it is confined to lanes 2,3 (and the ignored tail bytes)'. Also the carry-model rates for lane-1 bytes 2,3,5: for a single flipped bit b the R=0 collision rate is (1-2^-(32-b))^2 for 16<=b<=23, 1-2^-(32-b) for 24<=b<=31, (1-2^-(48-b))^2 for 40<=b<=47.

verdict.reasoning: The claim has two parts. (b) The carry-model rates: the byte-2 formula (1-2^-(32-b))^2 for 16<=b<=23 is wrong for b=16..22. Read against the C source (ZipperMergeAndAdd byte map: lane-1 own byte 3 -> byte 0 of lane 1's addend, b.3->B.0; byte 2 -> B.2; byte 5 -> B.3; partner bytes 4,6,7 -> A.1,A.4,A.6), the model omits the path where the carry chain at step A runs from bit b into byte 3 of v1[1] but stops before bit 32 (probability 2^-(24-b), not itself a failure): byte 3 changes by +-1, lands in byte 0 of the step-E addend, so the addend difference is 1-2^24+2^b (magnitude ~2^24) and its borrow reaches bit 32 of v0[1] (byte 4, which feeds v1[0] at F) with probability (2^24-2^b-1)/2^32 ~ 2^-8 independent of b. Corrected exact rate: 1 - [2^-(32-b) + (2^-(24-b)-2^-(32-b))(2^24-2^b-1)/2^32 + (1-2^-(24-b))2^-(32-b)] ~ 1-3*2^-(32-b) instead of ~1-2*2^-(32-b); at b=23 both coincide, which is why the proof-trails 2^16-key check (3 vs 2 expected failures at b=16) could not see it. Measured with an unmodified copy of the reference (sha256 fb316726..., vectors kExpected64 x65 and key2/33B reproduced by the reference and by my HashR(.,4); traced Update equals reference Update on 2^16 states), 2^26 random keys and fresh random 32-byte base messages per bit, single flipped bit b of lane 1, R=0: b=16..22 give z=-22.7,-32.2,-42.4,-61.5,-79.4,-95.8,-89.8 against the lemma's formula and |z|<=1.43 against the corrected one; b=23,24,28,31,40,44,47 agree with both (|z|<=1.43 except one b=31 sample at -2.96, re-run with seeds 21,22 and with an independent splitmix64 stream: -0.39,-1.32,+0.72; b=16 with splitmix64: -22.2 vs lemma, +0.14 vs corrected). In every row collisions = 2^26 - Afail - Efail exactly with 0 collisions despite an A-failure; I proved E-failure => non-collision (v0[0], mul0[0], mul1[0] unchanged, out'-out = zipA addend difference != 0) and that the E carry chain is exactly independent of the A chain (bits 16..31 of v0[1] after C are a bijection of key[1] bits 16..31, on which S and the addend bytes do not depend), so the 'independent carry chains' heuristic is unnecessary but the corrected formula still ignores collisions-despite-A-failure (0 observed in 14x2^26 trials, no proven bound). The 24..31 formula omits a (1-2^-(32-b))2^-(56-b) term (<=2^-25, unmeasurable); the 40..47 formula is exact. (a) The converse ('probability exactly 1 only if confined to lanes 2,3 and ignored tail bytes') is neither refuted nor proven: it is an existence statement over 2^128-1 differences; my witness search (2^20 keys max, seed 5) found a key with distinct R=0 outputs for all 659 differences tried (128 single bits of lanes 0,1; all 276 two-bit differences in lane-1 bytes 2,3,5; all 255 values of lane-1 byte 2; hardest: +2^16 after 87327 collisions; example bit 16: key {1a80428bb86efc2d,f46374061ab62ccf,7d1b4f76800515e1,87e6d22d51aa1004}, out 9fa5fb15955044eb vs 9fa5fb15955043eb). The remainder-packet layout and Permute in the lemma match the source; the multi-packet case was not measured. measured_rate_log2 = log2 of the measured R=0 non-collision rate for lane-1 bit 16 (3077/2^26). proofVerdicts.lemma: Lemma 3 (one-step separation). For an additive difference delta != 0 in lane i of the packet from equal states: (a) lo32(v1[i]) differs iff lo32(delta) != 0; the high halves differ iff hi32(delta)+carry != 0 mod 2^32 (always if hi32(delta) not in {0, 2^32-1}; iff carry when hi32(delta)=0; iff no carry when hi32(delta)=2^32-1). (b) Since 32x32->64 products are exact integers, a'H - aH = (a'-a)H vanishes iff H=0: mul0[i] changes iff lo32(delta) != 0 and H = hi32(v0[i]) != 0; mul1[i] changes iff the high half of v1[i] changes and L = lo32(v0[i]+mul1[i]) != 0. (c) For one-packet messages (|M|<=32, full or remainder path) and a uniform key, H and L are independent uniform 32-bit words: P[H=0]=P[L=0]=2^-32, P[H=L=0]=2^-64; for |M|=32, P[carry]=lo32(delta)/2^32 exactly and the carry is independent of L. Exact corollary: mul0[i] is unchanged for every key with hi32(key[i]) = hi32(init0[i]); mul1[i] for every key with lo32(key[i]) = lo32(init0[i]) ^ (-lo32(init1[i]) mod 2^32).

proofVerdicts.lemma: Lemma 4 (silenced trails), rigorous part. A multiply is active if an operand differs; a trail is silenced if every active multiply has exactly one differing operand and its co-operand is 0 (then all 8(R+1) products coincide, mul0/mul1 never differ, the difference lives in (v0,v1)). (a) The message Update activates >= k_msg(delta) = #{i: lo32(delta_i)!=0} + #{i: hi32(delta_i) not in {0,2^32-1}} >= #{i: delta_i != 0} >= 1 multiplies for every key, each with one differing operand; for one-packet messages P[message Update silenced] <= 2^(-32 k_msg(delta)) <= 2^-32. (b) On a silenced trail round 1 activates >= 2 multiplies in two different lanes. (c) Every later round activates >= 1. (d) A silenced trail through Update + R rounds activates >= R+2 multiplies (R>=1), each needing a zero co-operand. The bound covers only the silenced class: not product coincidences a'H'=aH with both operands differing, and not trails where the multipliers differ but the difference never reaches lane 0 or cancels inside tau (the observed R=1 collisions are of that kind).

proofVerdicts.lemma: Lemma 1 (closed form, R=1, one packet). With A_i=(C1_i^swap32(k_i))+C0_i+m_i, B_i=(C0_i^k_i)+C1_i, M0_i=C0_i^(lo32 A_i * hi32(C0_i^k_i)), M1_i=C1_i^(lo32 B_i * hi32 A_i), X0=B0+f0(A0,A1), X1=B1+f1(A0,A1), Z2=B2+f0(A2,A3), Z3=B3+f1(A2,A3), Y0=A0+f0(X0,X1), Y1=A1+f1(X0,X1), U0=Y0+M0_0+swap32(Z2), W0=X0+M1_0, T=Y1+M0_1, U1=T+swap32(Z3), W1=X1+M1_1, a=W0+f0(U0,U1), b=W1+f1(U0,U1), v=U0+f0(a,b): H_1(m) = a+v+[M0_0^(lo32 U0*hi32 X0)]+[M1_0^(lo32 W0*hi32 U0)]. Here f0(x,y)=[x.b3,y.b4,x.b2,x.b5,y.b6,x.b1,y.b7,x.b0], f1(x,y)=[y.b3,x.b4,y.b2,y.b5,y.b1,x.b6,y.b0,x.b7]. proofVerdicts.lemma: Slice lemma. If for every fixing of the other key bits a byte quantity Q = phi(kappa)+e(kappa) mod 256 with phi a bijection of one key byte kappa (a byte of some k_i, or of A2/A3, which are bijective images of k2/k3) and e(kappa) in {0..r}, then Pr[Q=v] <= (r+1)/256, with equality 1/256 when r=0. Applications used: bytes of A_i uniform; Z3.b7, U1.b3, b.b0 bijective in A2.b7; Z3.b3 bijective in k3.b3; U1.b1 bijective in A2.b6; Z3.b5 bijective in A2.b6; U1.b0 via k3.b5 (r<=2), U1.b2 via k3.b4 (r<=3), U1.b4 via k3.b7 (r=1), U1.b5 and b.b3 via A2.b4 (r=1,2), Z3.b6 via k3.b4 (r<=2).

Derived on paper (README section 1): (a) a mul word can never carry a key-independent additive difference after a product-XOR (would need P1^P2 = 2^63, impossible for 32x32-bit products), so any cancellation must be v0[0] against v1[0] with both mul words equal, which forces the lane-0 v0/v1 words and q[0] to be clean at the start of the last round; (b) the complete budget of differences the last round's two ZipperMerge additions can deliver from lane 1 into the sum: out2-out1 = d4*(2^8+2^40) + (d6+d0)*2^32 + d7*2^48 + d1*2^8 (d_k = byte differences of lane 1's v1 after step A); (c) traced backwards through Permute/swap32 and the message-step ZipperMerge to last-packet bytes that avoid every lane-0/1 multiply: lane 3 byte 2 (+delta) and lane 3 byte 1 (-delta) deliver +delta*2^32 to v0[0] and -delta*2^32 to v1[0]. Carry-event accounting gives Pr[collision] = (1-delta/256)^6 (carries inside v0[3] are harmless because they survive swap32 and the addition exactly). Tested every derived pair at 2^26 keys (3 threads, xoshiro256** keys), with R=0 sanity pairs (lane-1 analogue, predicted (255/256)^4), single-byte controls, a random base, 31/63/64-byte lengths, a 4-byte family-(ii) pattern, and an exhaustive sweep of all 1984 two-byte +-1 patterns of the last packet at 2^16 keys. Per-collision tally of which lane-0 words differ confirms the mechanism.-R1

workflowProgress.label: repro:Evolutionary (mu+lambda, mu=lambda=14, tournament selection, <=3 members per xor-difference, hall of fame of 16 distinct differences, key set of 2^16 renewed every 40 generations with population + hall of fame re-scored) hill-climb over message pairs (m, m2) at R=3, difference confined to the last 32-byte packet (32 B, 64 B) or the 16 remainder bytes (48 B), all base bytes mutable, same mutation set as hillclimb-R2 plus a --forbid option. NEW objective built for an additive output: for every k the counts of keys whose output xor-difference is zero in the LOW k bits (lo-k) or the HIGH k bits (hi-k), and of keys with |out2-out1| < 2^(64-k) (add-k, ideal 2^(1-k)); score 'lo' = 8 log2(1+c64) + sum over k in {8,12,16,20,24,28,32} of the one-sided Poisson deviance (bits, capped 400) of lo-k, hi-k, add-k vs ideal; 'mix' = 'lo' + 0.72 max(0, energy-128) where energy = sum of z^2 over the 64 xor + 64 additive difference bits (null 128+-16). Plus a SYSTEMATIC single-byte sweep at R=3: every byte position of the difference region x every xor value 1..255 (32 B: 8160 candidates, 48 B: 4080) on one random base at 2^15 keys. Runs (1 thread each): sweep32, sweep48; S1 32 B 'lo' 1081 s seeded with A/B/sum-cancellation/weak-key pairs (22784 evals x 2^16 keys); S2 48 B 'mix' 1081 s (17896 evals); S3 32 B 'mix' with byte 29 FORBIDDEN seeded from the best non-29 sweep entries (3764 evals, 213 s); S4 64 B 'mix' 330 s (7346 evals). Out-of-sample re-measurement with fresh splitmix64 key seeds, 3 threads: S1 top 1 at 2^28 (R=2..4) and 2^26, S1 top 2/3 distinct differences at 2^26 (R=3,4), S2 top 1 and S3 top 1 at 2^24 (R=3,4), and a designed 64 B pair (byte 29 difference in the second packet) at 2^25 (R=2..4, 1 thread). hh_r.c byte-identical to angles/structured-differences (cmp); ./hh_test reproduces all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4 (run this session).-R3

workflowProgress.label: repro:Analytic cancellation in the final lane-0 sum v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0] at R=3, derived on paper first (README section 2) and checked mechanically. (1) Last-round analysis for any R: only lane 0, q[0]=swap32(S.v0[2]), q[1]=swap32(S.v0[3]) and the four lane-1 words of the entering state matter; the budget out2-out1 = d4(2^8+2^40)+d6 2^32+d7 2^48+e4 2^8+e6 2^32+e7 2^48 on X=v1'[1], E=v0''[1] leaves X bytes 2,3,5 and E bytes 0..3,5 FREE (never reach lane 0), and has two unabsorbed carry routes (v0''[0].b5->v1''[0].b3 weight 2^24, v0''[0].b2->v1''[0].b2) that invalidate sumcancel-R2's literal family (ii); corrected family-(ii) pair predicted at 2^-4(255/256)^5. (2) A new cancellation mechanism, q-cancellation: a key-independent difference in S.v1[0] cancelled in step A of lane 0 by -swap32 of a difference in S.v0[2] before any multiply; realizable at R=1 by lane 1 byte 0 (+1) with lane 2 byte 3 (-1), and lane 1 byte 1 (+1) with lane 2 byte 1 (-1), predicted 2^-16..2^-17 (lane-1 pollution budget), single halves predicted 0. (3) R=3: pulling the last-round conditions (S2 lane 0 clean, S2.v0[2] clean, budget) back through round 2 shows all eight mul words must be clean after round 1 up to per-byte coincidences; every packet byte pollutes a mul word of its lane in the packet step and that pollution is full-width after round 1, so no designed R=3 trail exists and the cheapest confinement events are 2^-24 (lane 1) / 2^-32 (lanes 2,3; the L2 silencing of the lane-3-byte-0 channel). route3.py (byte-level K/pollution tracer) reproduces the measured S1/S2 word-equality fractions. (4) Measurable R=3 effect = top-bit bias; S3 per-word attribution shows the mechanism (narrow S2 lane 0 + the 0.153 bias of bit 63 of 32x32 products). Driver sc3.cpp on hh_r.c (byte-identical to the panel copy; ./hh_test passes all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4) records per key at r=0..4 collisions, per-bit z (xor and additive), top-16 partial collisions, word-equality fractions at S0/S1/S2, the R=2 conditions on S1, the R=3 conditions on S2 (L0,Q0,M01,M11,X467,E467,BUD,ALL3), S3 per-word bit-63/width statistics. Runs (3 threads, nice 10, xoshiro256** keys): 32 single bytes x 2^20 (salt 1); 992 two-byte patterns (all a<b, signs ++ and +-) x 2^18 brief; bytes 29 and 24 x 2^26 on a fresh stream (salt 3); q-cancel pairs + 3 controls x 2^24; family-(ii) pairs x 2^20.-R3

workflowProgress.label: repro:Weak-key / weak-state conditioning at rounds 0, 1 AND 2 (R=3 target), single 32-byte packet, base b4a9f0039dfdf1097584bf1b16743255b343b39646ca5b5d8d52227d6c9bd270. Driver wk3.cpp on hh_r.c (round-configurable copy of the reference C; ./hh_test reproduces all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the 33-byte key2 vector at R=4; --selftest: my Update == HighwayHashAbsorb, exact InvUpd(Update)==id, Rnd == HighwayHashRound, 0 mismatches on 100000 random (key,packet)). Two sampling models: (1) KEY model: key uniform, round-0 conditions A<i>=H<i>@0 / B<i>=L<i>@0 as linear pins, round-1 conditions by byte-wise DFS over 4 key bytes (weakkey-R2 knob map); (2) UNIFORM-STATE model (new): the 1024-bit state S1 after the last packet is uniform (long-message heuristic), round-1 conditions set directly on S1, round-0 conditions met by BACKWARD knobs through the exact inverse packet Update (H: hi32(mul1[i]), L: lo32(v0[i]), W: lo32(v1[i]), V: hi32(v1[i]) of S1), round-2 conditions by FORWARD knobs (H: hi32(mul1[i]), L: lo32(mul1[i]) with round-1 settings re-applied, W: lo32(mul0[i]), V: hi32(mul0[i])); S0 = InvUpd(S1,packet1), message 2 absorbed from the same S0. Conditions on the entry state T of Update r: H<i>@r hi32(T.v0[i])=0 (silences mul0[i]), L<i>@r lo32(T.v0[i]+T.mul1[i])=0 (silences mul1[i]), W<i>@r lo32(T.v1[i]+T.mul0[i]+lanes[i])=0, V<i>@r hi32(same)=0. DFS takes the first solution from a random start (approximately uniform inside the class); EVERY sample is re-verified on the reference forward computation (verify_fail=0 in all reported runs). Per sample both messages absorbed, rounds applied one at a time; at R=0..4: full collisions, lane-0-words-equal, per-output-bit XOR z, mean HW, per-word AND per-byte equality of all 16 state words (the byte map is what exposes the trail). Model validation: state vs key model agree (A3: R=2 2^-9.96 vs 2^-9.99 here vs 2^-9.86 weakkey-R1; A3&H1&L2: R=2 0.973 vs 0.983 vs 0.980; R=3 bias 0.95 vs 0.97 vs 0.968 per sqrt N). New trick: the unsilenceable round-1 mul0[3] (both operands carry the difference) is made KEY-INDEPENDENT by H3@1 & W3@1 (operands 0*0 vs 1*2^16 -> constant bit-16 flip), then round-2 lane-1 multiplies silenced (H1@2, L1@2). 1 thread per run (host load average ~350), 2^10..2^18 samples.-R3
